explanation: The pole reads the identity of the current token through a fixed layer-0 key centred on markup and code identifiers: '<X' angle-bracket tokens and '>' fire up to 3.5-4.1 on code (4-5x the 0.82 maximum anywhere in the web scan), and on plain prose the firing inventory is that same token-id set and its nearest surface forms - CamelCase continuations ('Locker' in 'BitLocker', 'Discover' in 'OutreachDiscovering', 'Ball' in 'Pendulum Ball'), '>' after a tag-name piece, ' &', bare capitalised title words (0.82 as the first token of a text), and the word-internal pieces 'able'/'ination'/'occus'/'iers'/'ians' - plus a residual set of ordinary polysyllabic words (' must', ' through', ' proper', ' related', ' during', about 0.2) that share the same embedding region with no obvious semantic link; each token's strength is fixed by its id, so context and position move it by at most about 0.1 apart from the first-token boost. Explicit exclusions a detector must apply: the space-initial spelling of the same string is a different token id and is inert (' able' 0.00 vs 'able' 0.46; ' <T' 0.00 vs '<T' 4.1; ' Test' 0.08 vs 'Test' 0.82), the stems are inert ('market', 'Discrim', 'row', 'Bit' all about 0), other derivational suffixes are inert ('ology', 'ance', 'ment', 'ness', 'ity', 'ation' all < 0.1), and common function words (' the', ' of', ' and', ' is', ' to') are inert.

The pole is a one-token word-initial 'Mc' fragment detector: 'Mc' is the highest-activation token in the entire 151,936-token vocabulary (2.07 with the token alone at position 0) and every short word-initial Mc piece (' Mc', ' McB', ' McD', ' McInt', 'McC', ' McC', ' McA', ' McN', ' McGr', ' McGu', ' McL', ' McG', ' McK') fires at 0.65-1.41, while mid-length single-token Mc-words fire only ~0.6 and long complete Mc-surnames barely fire (' McCarthy' 0.09, ' McKay' 0.11); the following token is irrelevant - a bare ' Mc' before an ordinary word ('the Mc clan') fires as hard as before a surname - so this is a retrospective token detector, not name completion or lookahead. Its remaining activity is a fixed, graded token set rather than a lexical class (' diagnosis', ' NSW', ' Gospel', ' Judgment', 'Patrick', ' victory', ' Christmas', ' Wednesday', ' pulmonary', 'Luke', 'Cisco', '福', 'rootScope' fire at 0.5-1.4, while matched controls 'treatment', 'court', 'James', 'London', 'cardiac', 'bible' stay near the 0.13 ordinary-prose baseline; corpus frequency rho -0.04, wordfreq rarity rho -0.03, script, length and corpus-usage features all fail to predict the set), and it is disjoint from the verified negative pole, which is a two-token feature on the continuation tail after a short vowel fragment ('ster' after 'E'): this pole is silent on those tails (' Leod' 0.15, 'Av' 0.07) and the negative pole is silent on 'Mc'.

N869+ is a retrospective, essentially context-free detector of the layer-0 token PIECE that spells 'code' (token identity explains r2=0.98 of its variance, position 0%; neighbouring text shifts it only about +-0.3). Activation saturates at 0.75-1.2 of max on the standalone word in any case and any attachment ('code', 'Code', 'CODE', ' code', ' Code', '\tcode', '.code', '-code', '/code', '_code', '(code', '[code'), reaches 0.75-0.85 on its plurals ('codes', ' codes', 'Codes'), 0.45-0.55 on 'coded' and ' coding', 0.28-0.75 on compounds ('bytecode', 'barcode', 'postcode', 'codec', 'getCode', 'encoding'), 0.25-0.80 on the word for 'code' in other scripts ('代码', 'コード', '코드', 'código', 'codigo', 'код', 'קוד', 'kode', ' kod'), and 0.25-0.40 on the bare continuation pieces '-ode'/'-odes'/'-oded' that BPE produces when it splits a longer word, whatever that word means ('nematodes', 'diodes', 'Explode', 'bode', 'brooded'); 'Credit'/'credit' (0.29-0.48 of max) is the only non-'code' family that clears the 25%-of-max line. It is INACTIVE (below 0.25 of max) on everything else: programming vocabulary that does not contain the string (python, java, html, sql, password, software, program, hacker <=0.20), on single tokens that merely contain the letters 'ode' (' model' 0.06, ' mode' 0.02, ' Unicode' 0.01, ' nodes' 0.00, ' episode' 0.01), on buried forms (' vscode' 0.17, 'urlencoded'->' encoded' 0.23), and on the graded near-misses ' encoded' (0.21), 'credits' (0.22), ' encode' (0.19) and ' decode'/' decoded' (0.13), which sit just under the line; 99.5% of the 20,858 token types in the scan never exceed 0.13 of max. Operationally: predict a window ACTIVE only if its strongest token piece is one of the 'code' spellings above (the letters 'code' inside a larger single token, as in unicode, node, decode or vscode, do not count), and predict it INACTIVE otherwise.

L0/N1049- is a layer-0 token-embedding readout keyed to the diet/diagnosis word stems, not to nutrition as a topic: its strength is fixed almost entirely by the current token (97% token identity, 0% position) and the pole fires hardest at 2.0-4.0 on whichever single Qwen BPE piece spells the diet stem in that tokenisation - ' diet'/'diet'/' Diet' (2.5 alone, 2.9-4.0 in sentence context), ' diets' (2.1-2.4), ' dieta', and the 'iet' piece of a line-initial 'Diet' (3.2) - with a mid band of 0.6-1.6 on ' diag'/' diagnose'/' diagnosis'/' diagnoses'/' diagnostic(s)'/' DIAG'/'_diag', 'agnosis', ' Dietary'/' dietary' (0.9-1.9), ' nutrition'/' Nutrition' (0.8-1.3), ' budget' (1.2-1.4) and 'Di' (0.5-0.7). It is lexical and piece-level rather than semantic or topical: ' diet' fires just as hard in the political sense ('the Japanese diet debated the bill', 3.2) as in the food sense, health/food/disease words without those stems (' health', ' food', ' meal', ' disease', ' obesity', ' medical', ' doctor') and 'die'-initial near-misses (' die', ' diesel', ' dinner', ' digital', ' dialogue') stay at or below 0.25 in context, and the same word fires or not depending on Qwen's split - ' dietitian' (' diet'+'itian') reaches 3.5 while the spelling ' dietician' (' di'+'etic'+'ian') reaches only 0.34, and ' diets' reaches 2.4 while ' Diets' (' Di'+'ets') reaches only 0.5.

N1270's negative pole is a layer-0 retrospective token-identity gate over one sparse, lexically specific band of the token-embedding space, not a topic detector: the strength is a fixed property of the token form (token identity explains 97% of scan variance, 85-93% of input attribution sits on the peak token, and a token gives the same strength in any sentence), only ~120 of the 9,433 token types seen at least three times reach the 0.30 active line, and the forms that fire are whole-word content tokens in five adjacent neighbourhoods of that band - religion/doctrine (' religion' 0.83, ' religious' 1.02, ' spiritual' 0.60, ' sacred' 0.75, ' faith' 0.42, ' worship' 0.31, ' Jewish' 0.43, ' Islamic' 0.34, ' Muslim' 0.42, ' Jerusalem' 0.33, ' priest' 0.33/' priests' 0.43, ' pilgr-' 0.40), sectarian and foreign-affairs names (' Syria' 0.67, ' Israel' 0.55, ' Palestinian' 0.39, ' Hezbollah' 0.87, ' Turkey' 0.39, ' Erdoğan' 0.31), nation and place names that are not among the handful used most (' Norway' 0.72, ' Ireland' 0.62, ' France' 0.41, ' Germany' 0.72, ' Russia' 0.31, ' Japan' 0.31, ' Sweden', ' Lithuania' 0.75, ' Greece' 0.34), occupational and institutional abstract nouns, mostly in their plural or long form (' profession' 0.74, ' graduates' 0.65, ' colleges' 0.57, ' faculty' 0.35, ' colleagues' 0.54, ' Congress' 0.67, ' Democrat' 0.33, ' credentials' 0.38, ' subscription' 0.44, ' deposit' 0.43, ' constituents'), and a thin technical/physiological set (' serotonin' 0.83, ' symptoms' 0.40, ' ultrasound' 0.32, ' encrypted' 0.41, ' encryption', ' prototype' 0.40, ' functionality' 0.39, ' myfile' 0.65, ' .js' 0.25), with capitalised Latin stem fragments such as ' Krak' 0.49, ' Wroc' and ' Tür' 0.38 also firing on their own; predict INACTIVE (0.00-0.25) for function words, digits and whitespace runs (which drive the opposite pole), for the everyday concrete core (' water', ' dog', ' book', ' tree', ' car', ' table', ' window', ' kitchen', ' food', ' night', ' mother', ' child'), for the highest-frequency personal names and countries (' John' 0.00, ' David' 0.00, ' Mary' 0.00, ' Michael', ' James', ' Robert', ' Thomas', ' William', ' India' 0.00, ' China' 0.06, ' Brazil' 0.01, ' America' 0.16, ' Canada' 0.04, ' Australia' 0.00, ' Africa' 0.00, ' Asia' 0.00), and for the three families the previous hypothesis over-reached on, which are withdrawn: clinical/medical vocabulary (' cortisol' 0.14, ' oncologist', ' biopsy' 0.19, ' diagnosis' 0.02, ' tumor' 0.04, ' dose' 0.09, ' vaccine', ' physician', ' patient' 0.00, ' surgery' 0.00, ' nurse' 0.01 - a clinical sentence peaks at 0.16-0.21), camelCase and library-style code identifiers plus ordinary programming words (' getUserToken', ' ApiClient', ' parseConfig', ' GroupLayout', ' routeProvider', ' instancetype', ' minOccurs', ' function' 0.01, ' return' 0.01, ' null' 0.00, ' object' 0.00, ' array' 0.01 - a code sentence peaks at 0.08), and diacritic/CJK word-forms as they tokenise in prose ('Kraków' gives Kr+ak+ów 0.08, '谢谢' 0.00, ' café' 0.12, ' Zürich', ' São' 0.00, ' señor', ' 한국'); predict inactive too for most same-field near-misses (' professor' 0.00, ' university' 0.00, ' school' 0.00, ' job' 0.04, ' career' 0.00, ' college' 0.03, ' charge' 0.11, ' business' 0.08, ' mosque' 0.09, ' temple' 0.01, ' church' 0.29, ' bishop' 0.09, ' God' 0.05, ' sin' 0.09, ' statute' 0.00, ' regulation' 0.11, ' audit' 0.00, ' invoice', ' portfolio' 0.00, ' insurance' 0.00, ' committee' 0.00, ' staff' 0.18, ' senator' 0.03, ' parliament', ' court' 0.00, ' hospital' 0.00, ' doctor' 0.02), so do not predict a new member of a field by analogy; outside these five neighbourhoods the active set is idiosyncratic and topic does not decide it (e.g. ' cave' 0.50, ' cloud' 0.42, ' desert' 0.43, ' recess' 0.50, ' crew' 0.37, ' thoughts' 0.40, ' mentioned' 0.40, ' questioned' 0.35, ' truth' 0.33 fire while their everyday neighbours do not). Structurally the firing condition is a SwiGLU conjunction - gate projection positive AND up projection negative - so a clinical word (' cortisol': g +0.14, u -1.20) or a code identifier (' getUser': g +0.05) is up-negative but gate-flat and misses the wedge that its field neighbours enter.

Layer-0 subword bigram detector: fires on a word-internal continuation token (no leading space) such as 'ley', 'PE', 'uk', 'RA', 'w', 'rie', 'ry', 'pose', 'aler', 'ale', 'rah', 'to', 'TE', '4' when the immediately preceding token is a short word-start fragment ending in P/p or h/H (' P', 'P', ' Ch', 'ch', ' Sch', ' H', ' Ph', ' Sh', ' AP', ' MP', ' EP', 'Sup', ' Rip', ' Ash'); it stays near zero when the same continuation follows any other fragment or whole word (' K'+'rie', ' Kings'+'ley', ' Prop'+'ose', 'Q'+'450'), when the continuation carries a leading space (' P'+' w'), on the prefix token itself, and on continuations outside the set ('ola', 'ina', 'ett', 'ford'), independent of wider context.

N2560's negative pole marks the end of a written quantity: it peaks when the current token is a short (at most 3 characters) alphabetic or unit-symbol fragment that cannot continue a hexadecimal numeral - any single letter g-z, or unit tokens such as ' m', 'mm', 'nm', 'km', 'h', '%', 'x', '×' - and the immediately preceding token ends in a digit ('The cable is 25 [[m]] long.' 1.55, 'rose 65[[%]]' 0.55, '#519[[m]]' 1.19, 'loc3[[g]]' 1.07); it fires much more weakly when the quantity is a spelled-out number ('twenty [[m]]' 0.67, 'twelve [[m]]' 0.44) and not at all after a non-quantifier ('the [[m]]' 0.00), so 90.8% of the 371 scan peaks at or above 0.25 x max sit on a token whose predecessor ends in a digit (13x the base rate, and 37x once the short non-hex-token condition is added). It is silent when the next token could continue the numeral or hex run (digits, and the hex letters a-f: '25 f' 0.00, '#519f' 0.00), when the preceding token is letter-final ('2s m' 0.31), and when the next token is a full word ('25 metres' 0.00, '65 percent' 0.06); its mirror-image positive pole fires on exactly those hex-letter fragments (a-f: 'fad', 'bbc', 'df') inside numeric/hex/ID strings, which multi-character abbreviations fire is token-specific (mm, nm, km, hr, min, mol do; ms, GB, MHz do not), and the residual 9% of scan peaks are unexplained word-internal continuation fragments ('acter', 'ycl', 'opol').

Layer-0 single-token (unigram) detector for a fixed, semantically unrelated lexicon: it fires on the current token alone when that token is one of a specific set, strongest on 'monary' (the tail of cardiopulmonary/extrapulmonary, ~1.0), 'Classic' (no leading space), 'Jean', ' favorite'/' favourite', 'la' (S-la-ughters), 'StringRef', 'ties' (Six-ties), 'yth' (Fors-yth), 'au' (Nass-au), 'egade', ' NEGLIGENCE', ' steady', ' pulmonary', ' console', ' mening', 'oph' (es-oph-agitis), ' Manhattan', ' BOOST', and stays near zero on close synonyms or same-domain neighbours ('Modern', ' passion', ' stable', ' terminal', ' renal', ' hepatitis', ' gastr', 'Jan' only ~0.3). Surrounding context barely matters (the preceding token shifts strength by at most ~0.1-0.3 of max, e.g. ' JS' before 'StringRef' raises it), so the same trigger token fires in any sentence, register or language.

The positive pole is a retrospective unigram detector for a clustered family of relational/generic-vocabulary tokens: it fires on the current token when that token is a spatial or relational marker (around, through, within, behind, during), a temporal term (Friday, days, weeks, quarterly, today), a pronoun, number or light auxiliary (she, there, did, five), or a generic relational predicate (began, announced, gave, told, love, sits, runs, guide, support, range, interest, crowd), and stays near zero on semantically narrow concrete nouns (museum, pizza, river, senator, planet, banana) and specific action verbs (wrote, danced, scored, fell, raised). The same neuron's negative pole fires on exactly those concrete-specific tokens (princess, mat, fraud, Neil), confirming the generic-vs-specific distinction it encodes; the boundary is fuzzy (house/table drive it weakly, while time/always/get/every do not), reflecting an embedding-neighborhood detector rather than a crisp semantic class.

Retrospective layer-0 token detector: the negative pole reads the current token's own embedding and fires in proportion to how close that token sits to the 'method / technique / management' noun cluster - method(s), technique(s), methodology/ies, management, treatment(s) and business(es) at 1.1-2.2 of its 2.22 max, with practice(s), strategy/ies, approach, procedure, therapy, software, enterprise, company, style(s), algorithm and firm at 0.35-0.85 - including plural, capitalised, camelCase/identifier and translated forms ('Method' in makeNativeMethod, '_methods', 'метод', '方法', 'método', 'méthode'), at any position and largely regardless of the surrounding words. It stays near zero on near-synonyms that name a plan or a bare process rather than a practised way of doing something (process 0.02, plan 0.01, way 0.00, mode 0.00, framework 0.00, protocol 0.01) and on adjectival derivatives of the same stems (strategic 0.06, practical 0.09, procedural 0.12), and 'administration' (0.00) does not stand in for 'management' (1.64), so the pole tracks this specific embedding cluster rather than the general concept of a procedure or a technical/business register.

Layer-0 grapheme detector for the letter h in the token currently being read: the pole fires on any token whose surface string starts with h/H, whether it is a bare or short piece or a hyphen/space/punctuation-prefixed one ('-H' 4.02, '-h' 3.91, 'HP' 3.63, 'H' 3.53, ' H' 3.48, 'h' 2.52, 'hl' 3.12, ' Harvard' 2.26) or the word-initial h that BPE leaves inside a longer word ('historic' 1.60 in 'prehistoric', 'hood' 0.93 in 'boyhood'), reaching 1.1-4.4 of the 4.4 scan max for all but its ~9% most frequent h-words (' have' 0.24, ' his' 0.19, ' here' 0.30, ' how' 0.12, ' however' 0.03), while tokens whose h is not leading stay at the floor (medians 0.11 for h-after-one-letter pieces like ' sh', 'ch', 0.00-0.01 for ' the', 'this', 'which', and 0.000 for tokens with no h at all), with only a weak residual band when h ends a short piece (' unh' 1.5, ' pH' 1.35, 'oh' 0.53). It is retrospective and context-invariant (token identity explains 99.7% of variance, position 0%, 91% of the input attribution on the peak token, and the same token gives the same strength in any sentence), orthographic rather than lexical (the invented word 'hox' fires at 3.17 against 'glorx' 0.06), and zero-ablating it costs the model the continuation of the h-word just read ('oo' after 'Boo-H', 'od' after 'non-H', 'ick' after 'oak-h') rather than any fixed upcoming token, so it is not lookahead.

N3252+ is the weak positive half of the layer-0 chemistry-morpheme detector N3252- and has no family of its own: its strength is set by the token pair (previous piece, current piece) rather than by the current piece alone (held-out-document R2 0.93 for pairs seen in training versus 0.46 for the current piece, 0.29 for an additive model), and every activation above 0.36 of its 1.09 maximum sits where both SwiGLU factors are positive on that pair - a preceding piece on the gate row's chemistry side (the gate row's own top vocabulary tokens are 'ethyl', 'oxy', ' methyl', 'yl', 'hydro', '氯', '苯', 'amine') followed by a current piece that its up row rates positively. Its active set is therefore a memorised fragment-pair list inside rare, foreign, technical and code-identifier words ('</'+'TITLE' 1.09, ' phen'+'otyp' 0.95, ' AL'+'IVE' 0.92, 'ri'+'eger' 0.84, 'navbar'+'-toggle' 0.79, ' mal'+'igned' 0.78, 'eh'+'ives' 0.78, 'disple'+'asure' 0.73, 'kra'+'amp' 0.67, ' vari'+'ável' 0.73) that does not generalise by meaning, script or word class - 'genotypic' peaks at 0.10 where 'phenotypic' peaks at 0.85, 'Netanyahu' 0.05 and 'pharmacokinetics' -0.04 where 'Krieger' 0.84 - while ordinary prose (max 0.11), single-token technical words (' peptide', ' protein', ' enzyme', ' molecule') and every chemistry pair stay inactive (' phen'+'yl' -4.7, ' phen'+'ol' -1.3; 'yl', 'ethyl', 'oxy', ' methyl' are the negative pole's triggers and are never positive here).

This pole is a retrospective unigram detector for a capitalized word-onset token: it fires when the current token starts a word with an uppercase letter and belongs to an idiosyncratic embedding-defined set concentrated on past-tense/past-participle and modal verb forms (Made, Taken, Fell, Slept, Caught, Known, Established, Received, Filed, Submitted, Bought, Sent, Had, Saw, Should, May) plus scattered capitalized members (March, Unemployment, Gate, Dawn, Offer, and Sadd-/Fle-/Conf-/Dep-/Arr- onsets). The same stems lowercased (made, should, may, saddler), subword continuations (ler, ositions), and out-of-set capitalized tokens (The, He, Dogs, Monday, Zebra, Quantum, Eaten, Landed) stay at the near-zero floor (~0.03).

Layer-0 lexical key, not a meaning detector: the pole's strength on a text is the max over its tokens of a fixed per-token-type key, so the peak sits on that token, a long passage is active as soon as one key token appears anywhere in it, about 2% of the vocabulary is above the 0.32 activity threshold, and ordinary prose with no key token stays at or below ~0.2 (20 such sentences measured <=0.17). The interpretable head of the key is amount/degree vocabulary (' handful' 1.45 in a sentence, ' plenty' 0.98, ' plethora' 0.74, ' myriad' 0.77, ' quota' 0.71, ' minority' 0.51, ' majority' 0.49, ' few' 0.39, ' subtly' 1.11, ' passionate' 0.86, ' incapable' 0.69, ' capable' 0.59, ' questionable' 0.64, ' potentially' 0.97), with a semantically unrelated tail of individual tokens and word pieces firing just as hard (' pot' 1.04, ' potato' 0.49, ' mosquito' 0.55, 'caret' 1.14, ' tasty' 1.21, ' dorm' 0.89, 'expire' 0.55, 'epad' inside ' Notepad' 1.00, 'ika' inside ' Troika' 0.63, and scattered code or control identifiers such as 'TODO', 'getArguments' and 'ObjectId' near the threshold). Because the key belongs to the token type and not to the sense, ' handful' fires in 'a handful of them' (1.45) and in 'a handful at bedtime' (1.43), ' potential' fires in 'potential energy' and ' minority' in 'the minority party', while near-synonyms that are different tokens stay silent (' modicum' 0.00, ' dash' 0.02, ' pinch' 0.20, ' numerous' 0.08, ' abundance' 0.21, ' quantity' 0.13, ' many'/' much'/' several'/' number'/' amount' <=0.12, ' meticulous' 0.05, ' esoteric' 0.02); words fire only when the Qwen tokenizer emits a high-key piece for them - the mid-sentence space-prefixed ' handful' fires, a sentence-initial capitalised ' Handful' (tokenised 'Hand'+'ful') does not, and ' Notepad' fires through 'epad' while 'capability' 0.06, 'questionably' 0.05 and 'expires' 0.19 do not. Its negative pole is the mirror contrast: directional '-ward/-orth' tokens (' forward' -3.8, ' onward' -1.5, ' clockwise' -1.0) suppress the unit and so sit at 0 on this pole.

The positive pole is a layer-0 token detector for CHANNEL: it fires whenever the current token is the word 'channel' in its common BPE forms (' channel', '-channel', '_channel', 'Channel', 'channels', ' CHANNEL', 'channelId') or in translation ('通道', '频道', 'канал', 'kênh'), and it shows graded partial activation on a halo of tokens whose embeddings carry the same bounded-passage/connector sense (lane, passage, ford, crossing, tunnel, bridge, corridor, doorway, hatch, driveway, freeway, highway, dam, ditch, pavement, inlet, outlet, sink, junction, intersection, port, harbor, HDMI, adapter, plug, interface, viewport, iframe, beacon). Firing is retrospective and essentially token-driven — it is set by the current token's own embedding (the same token fires at a similar strength in different carriers and at different positions; open-route nouns like road, street, path and route and tube nouns like pipe, tube and duct stay below the halo level, and unrelated nouns like cabinet and table do not fire), with a few unrelated rare tokens from the same embedding neighbourhood (e.g. Renault, Chen, Refuge, Meadow) firing at the moderate halo level.

Layer-0 retrospective lexical detector: most drive (~65%) comes from the current token itself, with the preceding token adding at most ~0.15 of max. It fires strongest (>=0.7 of max) on a fixed set of word-forms (history/History, approach, problems, work/Working, Architecture, args, closing '}' and Chinese forms like 工作), moderately (0.2-0.55 of max) on morphological relatives (histories), modal/hedge and past-tense verbs (would, usually, might, could, probably, arrived, thinks) and related nominals (culture, research, American), and near-zero on function words and on close synonyms that are different tokens (heritage, method, labor, params, music, often, went). The Jacobian/promoted-token lens is incoherent (kurtosis ~3.8), so it reacts to input tokens rather than preparing specific upcoming tokens.

Retrospective layer-0 token-identity lookup, not a concept detector: strength is a fixed per-token value carried by the current token alone (token id explains 95.5% of the variance, position 0.3%; the peak token carries 0.84-1.00 of the integrated-gradient attribution, and a word scores the same in unrelated documents - ' clock' 1.21-1.34 over five occurrences, ' cash' 0.88-1.05 over nine, ' money' 0.66-0.83 over eleven, ' funds' 0.31-0.38 over six). A prompt is predicted ACTIVE only if it contains one of a closed set of word-forms - ' clock' (1.26) > ' cash' (0.96) ~ ' thrust' (0.94) ~ ' fauc' (0.83) ~ ' grounding' (0.81) > ' money' (0.71) > ' deficit' (0.60) > ' imperative' / ' Carmen' / ' Mon' / ' hunger' / ' brushing' / ' Ruby' / ' Rod' / ' Burg' / ' Pend' / ' conflict' / ' Cambridge' / ' mon' / ' Grammar' / ' conservative' / ' Monday' / ' fever' / ' revenue' / ' debt' / ' crisis' / ' Harvard' / ' funding' / ' dollars' / ' mill' / ' grammar' / ' military' / ' calcium' / ' muscular' / ' cough' / ' curves' / ' cavity' / ' strikes' / ' funds' / ' groundwater' (0.34-0.56, the 0.33 activity line is fuzzy by about +/-0.02) - and predicted INACTIVE for every other token, however close in meaning: 'water' 0.01 over 27 occurrences, 'time' 0.09, 'minute' 0.11, '$' 0.04, 'percent' 0.00, 'business' 0.12, 'company' 0.15, 'income' 0.15, 'spending' 0.17, 'dollar' 0.22, 'penny' 0.25, 'capital' 0.27, 'budget' 0.27. The lookup is on the surface form, so capital ' Pend' fires at 0.47 while the lowercase 'pend' inside 'pendulum' stays at 0.26, ' cashews' (tokenised ' cash'+'ews') fires at 0.88 while the single token ' cashier' stays at 0.16, and the opposite pole's vocabulary (' parts', ' group', ' whole', ' &', the bullet '·') is silent here.

The pole fires on a detached separator glyph: a single token that begins with a space and is made only of punctuation, detached from the word before it. Its strength is graded by glyph, strongest (0.5-1.0 of max) for the dash/slash/joiner family ' -', ' –', ' —', ' /', ' ·', ' |', ' >', ' --', ' +', ' •', ' :', ' ||', ' //' (and rarer forms such as ' ›', ' ―', ' ..', ' ---'), moderate (about 0.25-0.5 of max, sometimes just under the active threshold) for a detached ampersand, question or exclamation mark, semicolon, asterisk, equals sign, ellipsis or period, and at or below the active threshold for a detached comma, close paren, open bracket, quote, dollar sign, hash or backtick; the same glyph without its leading space (bare '-', '–', '/', as in 'well-known', '1925–2013', 'http://', 'Key:') is not detected at all. It is retrospective: the peak lands on the separator itself (76% of the input attribution is on that token), the token that follows it has no effect, the Jacobian-lens write just mirrors the same detached-glyph family (' >', ' ►', ' ..', ' ›', ' =>', ' :') and the measured ablation profile is unconcentrated (KL 0.006) - and it is about three times weaker when the separator starts a line after a newline (0.3-0.6) or about 40% weaker after another space-prefixed punctuation token (~1.0-1.2) than when it follows the last letter or digit of the left-hand item (1.4-2.0), which drops the weaker glyphs below the active threshold at a line start.

The pole is a layer-0 unigram (token-identity) detector: its strength is set by which token is being read, not by context or position (token identity explains 90% of the variance, position 1%), and it never fires on the frequent core of the vocabulary, staying at zero for function words, common content words and common names ('the', 'people', 'time', 'white', 'John', 'Paris' all measure <=0.06, and in the scan no token appearing 100+ times reaches the active threshold). It fires only on a sparse, idiosyncratic subset of the low-frequency long tail - rare words ('picnic', 'apartment', 'purple', 'blond', 'notebook'), proper names and places ('Sarah', 'Barbara', 'Rwanda'), technical and code/markup identifiers ('Npgsql', 'DataTable', 'dataGridView', '.md', '.rs') and unusual word pieces ('elix', 'oton', 'ologist') - and because many equally low-frequency words ('canyon', 'automobile', 'cuisine') stay at zero, predict active only when a marked long-tail token of these kinds is present, and inactive when every token is frequent core vocabulary.

A layer-1 bigram detector that fires on the second token of a few specific two-token pairs: most often the host token 'www' right after a URL scheme 'http://' or 'https://' (weak for a bare 'www', a missing scheme or most other subdomains such as 'docs' or 'mail'); also ' in'/' inside' right after a form of 'look' ('look in', 'looking in'; weak for ' at', ' into', or ' in' after other verbs); and 'L' right after 'OR' (as in 'ORL1'). The same tokens elsewhere, and the tokens before or after them, stay near zero.

A layer-1 spelling-fragment detector: the negative pole fires when the current token is one of a learned set of unusual letter fragments that occur as non-final pieces of names, acronyms and technical or foreign words - 'US' after 'V' (VUS), 'PT' after 'F' (FPTCs), 'MT' after 'E' (EMT), 'OP' after 'C' (COPD), 'AY' after 'H' (HAYNE), 'orm' after 'c' (cormorant), 'ank' after 'K' (Kankakee), 'uv' after 'ma' (mauvaises), 'æ' after 'hj' (hjælpe) - and on the name-onset tokens ' Hay'/'Hay' (Hayne, Hayao), ' Tay' (Tayyip), ' Bog' (Bogut) and ' Anderson', plus a smaller glue family of hyphen pieces ('-free' after 'risk'/'gun', '-engine' after 'reverse', '-' in 'X-Plane', the minus in '3*a - 7'). The trigger is the specific fragment, not the word's rarity or meaning: equally rare names and technical words with ordinary spellings (Kowalski, Nakamura, apoptosis, cholangitis), the same letters inside common words (bay, dorm, bank, corner, corn, GTP, 'haystack' as a single token) and ordinary prose all stay near zero, while the positive pole of the same SwiGLU unit fires on a disjoint fragment set ('ao' in Hayao, 'ot' in luaotfload).

N1675− fires on the lowercase function-word slots of Title Case spans: a lowercase function word (of, on, in, a, the, and, for, to, &, by, from, about) preceded within about four tokens by capitalized content words, peaking (2.2/2.31) on the prepositions, articles and conjunctions inside document titles, headlines, section headings, legal captions and quoted titles ('The Effects of Event Rate on a Cognitive Vigilance Task', 'The People of the State of Colorado', 'Eat & Drink Like a Local'), and more weakly on lowercase continuations inside capitalized names ('cci' in Carlucci 0.68, 'd' in P.3d 0.71, '.com' in ESPN.com 0.93); one capitalized word immediately before gives 0.88 of the full peak, a lowercase word immediately before cuts it to 0.29, and no capitalized word at all leaves 0.01. It is the case contrast that drives it rather than capital density or title position: the same words in ordinary lowercase prose sit at the floor (mean 0.001 and 0.02% active where no nearby content word is capitalized), a title embedded mid-sentence in prose still fires (2.28), while capitalizing the peak word itself (' Of' 0.11), every word (0.39) or ALL CAPS (0.04) goes quiet, no capitalized token anywhere reaches the active threshold (0/25,702), and the case of the tokens after the peak is irrelevant (a title-case prefix with a lowercase tail still fires at 1.67) - so the pole is retrospective on the capitalized run before it; its positive pole is the mirror, peaking (0.27-0.31 versus at most 0.15 in lowercase controls) on the blank line that ends a title-case heading line and on the first lowercase prose word after such a span.

The negative pole fires on a standalone operator glyph that is being used as an operator inside a symbolic expression: strongest on the space-prefixed plus ' +' and its LaTeX form '+\' (e.g. $a + b$, \kappa_{\mathrm{ex}}+\kappa_{\mathrm{in}}, 3 + 4, x = 42; y = x + 1;, f(a) + g(b)), then on ' -' and ' ='/'=\' at roughly a third to a half of that strength, with strength graded by how formulaic the immediate context is (highest inside $...$ math and backslash-command neighbourhoods, lower when the same expression is embedded in ordinary prose). It stays near zero when the glyph is not an operator of an expression: fused into a word, identifier, e-mail or URL ('C++', 'a+b', 'john+tag@example.com', 'h=315'), replaced by non-operator punctuation (a comma between the same operands), a lone LaTeX command or backslash, narrative or programming-discussion prose ('The story a + b is here.', 'In Python, a + b works.'), or another operator glyph (*, /, <, >, ^, ==, !=), which fire at most weakly (peak <= ~0.75, below the active range); it is a formula-operator detector, not a general symbol, punctuation or LaTeX detector.

The negative pole detects the English independent (absolute) possessive pronouns - mine, yours, hers, ours, theirs and archaic thine - as a closed word class: it peaks on the pronoun itself (about 5-11 activation, 45-100% of max) in any position or function (sentence-final, partitive 'a friend of mine', formulaic 'Yours sincerely'), and also when the word is spelled across two tokens (' O'+'urs' = Ours, 'h'+'ers' = hers, 'The'+'irs' = Theirs, ' th'+'ine' = thine). The determiner forms of the same paradigm (my, thy, your, her, our, their, his, its), the reflexive -selves forms and every other pronoun (one, ones, others, nobody, this, that) stay at or below 18% of max, while the homographic noun mine/mines (excavation) and its mining derivatives are a weak offshoot at 19-39% of max.

N2268- fires on the second token of a two-token unit that the preceding token has already committed to: a particle or preposition after an event/action word ('go about' 2.4, 'go over' 1.4, 'go around' 1.3, 'set up' 1.0, 'ready up' 1.1, 'plan up' 0.9, 'look about' 0.8), or the tail fragment of a word continued across two tokens ('Ke|isha' 1.1, 'Comp|iling' 0.7, 'Ans|ar' 0.6). Both tokens are required: the same particle after a determiner, pronoun or concrete noun is silent ('the up', 'hands up', 'table up', 'the word about' all ~0), the same verb with a particle outside the preferred set is near silent ('go back' 0.00, 'set out' 0.00, 'set aside' 0.00), and a non-event verb roughly quarters it ('put up' 0.37 vs 'set up' 1.16).

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a frequent local chunk: a common bigram or collocation (next+year, quarterly+revenue, pinch+of, guilty+to, second+half, water+boils, the+door, return+true), a fixed phrase (according+to, at+least+eight), a word-internal subword continuation (ochond+ria), or a sentence-initial content word after BOS (Add, Water, SELECT). The preceding 1-2 tokens do most of the causal work (single-token ablation effect ~1.0), so the identical peak token after an unrelated word stays near zero.

Predict active when the text names a place - a country, region, continent, city or nationality adjective (Germany, India, Japan, Europe, Berlin, British, African) anywhere earlier in the passage - and contains a national/institutional or civic content word (Federal, National, nation, America, US, Democratic, state, county, district, campus, college, hospital, restaurant, church); the peak lands on that word at 1.0-2.2, against 0.0-0.6 for the same sentence with a person, brand or generic location (Smith, Acme, the office, the venue) in the place slot. Words outside that class (table, car, money, water, peace, museum, market, factory) stay below 0.15 in every context tested, so a place name alone never fires the pole, and inside the class the place-free baseline is lowest for Federal, America, US, campus, college and hospital but reaches 0.6-0.9 for National, nation, restaurant, state and university in frames such as 'The committee mentioned the X during the meeting'.

This pole fires on the second token of a familiar, strongly associated two-token chunk: either the final subword piece that completes a multi-token word (e.g. MATERIAL+S, adapt+ability, mix+tures) or a word strongly predicted by the immediately preceding word (e.g. 'model' after 'mixed', 'with' after 'equipped', 'of' after 'pair'/'combination'/'look', 'parts' after 'replacement', 'delicious' after 'sound'). The same peak token preceded by an unrelated word, or a non-completing ending after the same prefix, does not activate it.

Fires on the head noun of an indefinite noun phrase 'a/an (+ optional adjectives) NOUN' when that noun is an abstract, adverbial-idiom head (manner, way, fashion, basis, extent, level, minimum/maximum, glance, sense, attempt, while, time, rate, perspective, distance, hurry, whisper, percentage, degree; also 'friend'), as in 'in an efficient manner', 'on a daily basis', 'to a lesser extent', 'at a minimum', 'in an attempt'. The indefinite article is required: replacing 'a/an' with 'the', 'this', 'such a', 'my', 'no', 'any' or dropping it cuts activity to <=0.2 of max, and concrete nouns after 'a' (car, dog, house, table, room, project, idea, doctor) stay near 0; a preceding adjective (similar, lesser, timely, different) often fires moderately (0.4-0.6 of max) ahead of the noun.

The pole fires on the word-final piece of a content word that the tokenizer happened to split: a token with no leading space that continues the word begun by the previous token, when that piece is a lexical chunk (str|aws 'straws', Con|dit 'Condit', dro|oling 'drooling', H|oles 'Holes', -ad|ult 'sub-adult', lace|w|ings 'lacewings', sys|root 'sysroot', hammer|head 'hammerhead', war|heads, well|head, Aqu|atic 'Aquatic', Expl|ode 'Explode', rep|resents 'represents', str|add|led 'straddled', Sp|ine 'Spine'), i.e. it tracks word-internal composition rather than the word: both pieces matter, so str+aws gives 2.5 of max while p+aws, m+oles and ch+root stay near zero. The identical word delivered as one whole token ('strips', 'holes', 'adult', 'pooling', 'lacewing', 'ahead', 'overhead', 'string', 'aquatic'), or as two spaced words ('sys root' 0.49, 'lace wings' 0.16), peaks below 0.25 of max, as do split tails that are productive grammatical suffixes ('ing', 'tion', 'ness', 'ent(s)'); 'head'/'heads' are the one piece that also fires as a spaced token after a content-word modifier ('hammer head' 1.05, 'long head' 0.88, 'the head of' only 0.32).

Layer-1 word-identity detector for the English lexeme REACH: the pole is strongly active (peak 2.6-5.7 against a 1.12 activity line) at any position that spells the word - ' reach', ' Reach', ' reaches', ' reached', ' reaching', ' Reached', the same word split across a token boundary ('Re'+'aches' about 9.2, 'RE'+'ACH' about 11.2), and compounds that leave 'reach' as its own token (overreach about 6.0-9.6, outreach about 2.0-2.4) - whatever the sense (motion verb, noun of extent or influence, the idioms 'within reach' and 'out of reach', and a bare mention of the word all peak alike), while words that merely contain 'reach' as a substring (reachable about 1.1-1.8, unreachable about 2.1) stay above the line but far weaker. It is neither a semantic nor an orthographic detector: the spelling neighbours 'each', 'teach', 'beach', 'speech', 'catch' and the extent synonyms 'extent', 'range', 'span', 'scope', 'breadth', 'attain', 'achieve' stay in the 0.1-0.5 background, only 'stretch'/'extend'/'extension' form a weak 0.5-1.9 ring that straddles the activity line, and a preceding extent modifier ('long', 'wide', 'broad', 'far', 'extended') raises the peak by about 1-1.5 but never drops it below about 2.5.

L2/N202+ fires on the token that completes a two-part compound name: the head (second) element of a nominal compound in prose ('search button', 'shift key', 'settings page', 'author page', 'Patriot Act', 'hand-foot syndrome'), a quoted label placed before such a head ('"red" button' fires, bare 'red button' does not), and, in code, the final CamelCase/snake_case component of an identifier ('...FolderJoinPolicy', '...CertificateRequest', '...VpnSitesClient', 'priceCtrl', 'readRecords'). Predict inactive: the same head token after a determiner, possessive or attributive adjective ('the button', 'his button', 'the red button'), the earlier components of the same compound ('Shared'/'Folder'/'Join' = 0.00), and compounds whose head is an ordinary object noun that rarely heads compound terms ('search dog', 'search chair', 'search door' stay about 0 even after a noun).

L2/N287+ is a two-token unit detector: the current token is only weakly predictive alone, and the pole peaks on the token that completes a word or number whose opening piece was the immediately preceding token, glued with no space at the join. Its dominant, most reproducible case is the digit pair '5' -> '4'/'5'/'6' (the numerals 54/55/56, e.g. '56-year-old', 'Port=5432', and the interior of '5555'), with a lexically narrower second family of word-final pieces (Ġf+'umble', ĠMar+'lon', Ġblue+'prints', Ġvent+'ral', ĠR+'ourke', Ġd+'ags', F+'***'); it is predicted inactive when the same token follows a different partner (Ġm+'umble', Ġrib+'osomal', 5 followed by 0/7/8/9), when the same word is one token or is split by a space ('Mar lon', 'blueprint'), and for any token in isolation.

This pole fires on the completion-side token of a locally highly constrained bigram: most strongly on a single-character separator (the standalone space immediately before a digit, ( right after range, > closing a tag, or the space after = or >) where the preceding token opens a slot with a nearly determined filler such as a number after to, by, at, =, >, range, or a numbered name like Apollo, and at mid strength on the fixed second word of a memorized phrase (than after greater, of after capital, bank after central, noon after at). The same separator or function word in an unconstrained context (a space before a non-number, of after ordinary nouns, than after other comparatives, ( after other verbs) drives little or no activation, which beats a pure token-identity account; weak blips on ordinary content words (announced, he, triangle, began) are acknowledged leftovers near baseline.

The negative pole fires when a possessive or existential phrase attributes a mental/conceptual entity to a subject: its peak (1.0-3.0, against a ~0.55 determiner floor) lands on the noun of 'have/has/had/gain/give/provide/possess (a|an|the|no|any) N' when N names a content or faculty of mind - idea, insight, understanding, sense, mind, thought, theory, hypothesis, concept, notion, claim, belief, opinion, view, perspective, interpretation, definition, principle, assumption, taste, eyes, ears ('She has an insight' 2.34, 'She has a claim' 2.68, 'She has a theory' 1.00, 'She gained insight' 1.76, 'has a sense of humour' 2.80). The same nouns only predicated or discussed stay silent ('The idea was good' 0.00, 'The theory is wrong' 0.00, 'We discussed the idea' 0.16, 'Their understanding grew' 0.09), a possessive phrase over a physical or non-mental noun reaches only the determiner's 0.5-0.6 ('She has a car' peaks at ' a' 0.57 while 'car' is 0.00), and the leftovers are a few physical tokens that sit in the same embedding region (hammer 1.45, windshield 1.21, skull 0.84, 'eur' inside 'aneurysm' 1.4) plus 'claim', which fires 0.6-1.1 even outside the frame.

The pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a memorized two-token chunk from a narrow inventory: blow/blew/back-forms + up; bump/crash/rush/walk/run + into; white/black/brown/blind + man; Big + Bang/House; title-case Back + To; Banach + space; background + -color/-position; Blues + cript; and continuations of split b-initial stems (bak|grunn, bas|emen, Ban|ach, Bak|ayaro, back|garden/pedal). The identical completion after a different head stays silent (grew/fixed/broke + up; burst/step/look/drive + into; tall/big/dark/deaf/young + man; White + House; foreground + -color; Hilbert/parking + space), as do b-initial heads outside the inventory (brave knight, Brooklyn Bridge, batter/Bundt, bootstrap); the licensing head can sit several tokens back (back it/them up; backed up the truck into).

The pole fires on the token that completes a two-token predicate unit built on a form of 'make' or 'keep' - the particle of a phrasal verb ('make up' 2.1, 'keep up' 3.6-4.6, 'make out' 1.4, 'make with' 1.1-2.1, 'keep with' 2.4), the resultative adjective the verb selects ('make good' 4.5-4.9, 'make ready' 3.3-3.7, 'make better' 2.3-3.1, 'make worse' 1.4) or the light-verb noun ('make peace' 2.3-3.0, 'make time' 1.5-1.6, 'make do' 3.2) - and it is silent on the verb's ordinary object NPs and on grammaticalised continuations: 'make sure' is 0.00 at all 29 occurrences in the 200k-token scan, 'make sense' 0.45, 'make use' 0.39, 'make known' 0.1, 'make careful' 0.1, 'keep track' 0.1, 'keep quiet' 0.2, and determiners or pronouns that open the object ('make the/it/them/him/their/people', 'keep the/it/them') drive the opposite pole to -3.0 to -6.5. Both halves of the pair are necessary: ' good' after feel/look/seem/very/a stays at 0.16 and ' up' after look/hold/pick/set/give/put at 0.11-0.46 ('get up' only 1.20), tokenizer-split compounds are not enough ('over'+'come', 'black'+'board', 'sun'+'light' 0.13; 'zinc electrode' 0.25), and ' of' two tokens after 'make' fires only when the middle token is 'sense' ('make sense of' 2.6-2.8, 'make use of' 0.9; ' of' after a time quantity like 'years of' stays at 0.8-1.4, at or below the 1.21 active threshold).

Fires retrospectively on the completion token of an explicit discourse-linking construction that ties the current clause to prior text (And,/So,, but also, as well as, As a result of, and equivalents such as Also/Additionally/Unlike/Later/Ini/nao), requiring both the partner word(s) and a preceding completed clause; the same head token without its partner or as a non-linking use is inactive.

This pole fires retrospectively on the token that completes a strongly-cued local chunk: a subword piece continuing a split (usually rare or technical) word (hy+pos, pron+eness, G+yll, McPh+erson, Ph+on, Ty+len) or the second word of a frozen collocation (public+service, Public+Affairs, Blood+glucose/sugar). Near-misses that stay near zero: the same tail piece after a weakly-cueing prefix (ty+pos 1.08 vs hy+pos 4.12; Gen+etic ~0), the same morpheme merged into one common token (happiness), or a free word combination (public park, sea spray). Graded detector: common words completing the same way fire weakly (typos 1.08) rather than zero.

This positive pole is a retrospective, graded detector of two-token binding: it peaks on a token that completes a unit opened by the token immediately to its left, either the next piece of a word the tokenizer split ('As' after 'PD' in PDAs, 'sons' after 'Daw' in Dawsons, 'ius' after 'Maurit', 'us' after 'sa' in sausages, 'va' after 'Pur') or the second element of a multi-token name or fixed expression ('Britain' after 'Great', 'Alberta' after 'University of', 'Violence' after 'Family', 'China' after 'Greater', 'Lakes' after 'Great', 'recently' after 'until', 'out' after 'grew', 'well' after 'may', 'A' after 'David'). The same word after a determiner, preposition or unrelated modifier ('modern Britain', 'the college in Alberta', 'may still', 'came out', lowercase 'violence') sits at or below zero, so the pole tracks how strongly this model binds the pair rather than the token's identity, frequency or surprisal (correlation with the model's own next-token log-probability is -0.005 over 20k natural-text tokens, with entropy -0.03, with token frequency 0.06); it is selective rather than a general compound detector, since 'New York', 'White House' and 'University of Toronto' are inactive while 'Great Britain', 'Great Lakes' and 'University of Alberta' are active.

L2/N3729+ is a retrospective, sparse lexical-binding detector: it fires at token t only when the two-token string (token t-1, token t) is a fixed string the model has memorized, and it stays at the floor when the same slot is filled by a semantically equivalent but unmemorized alternative, so the pole tracks the exact pair and never either token alone. The memorized keys cluster on J-initial stems plus a high-frequency continuation ('Journal of' 5.7, 'jug of' 3.0, 'jazz of' 2.0, 'jar of' 1.9, 'junction of' 1.9, 'Justice of' 2.7, 'j'+'ourn' in journald 4.0, 'J'+'.' 3.0, 'jquery'+'-'+'3' 2.2, 'java'+'Script' 1.8), with a minority of non-J keys ('Rio Grande' 1.6, 'Jackie Chan' 1.5, 'should I'/'should he' 1.5, 'Heisen'+'berg' 1.2, 'Index of' 1.3); parallel strings outside the key set sit at the floor ('bottle of' 0.08, 'report of' 0.04, 'blues of' 0.17, 'jacket of' 0.12, 'New York' 0.02, 'United Nations' 0.03, 'M.' 0.15, 'Schwar'+'zen' 0.08), so a labeler should mark text active only for a listed key pair or an exact repetition of one, not for its family.

N3833- is a sparse, retrospective two-token-chunk detector: it peaks on the second token of a pair this model stores as one lexical unit, either the continuing piece of a word Qwen's tokenizer split (' Concor'+'de', ' disc'+'ursive', ' dispos'+'als', ' dis'+'joint'+'ed', ' part'+'ing') or the second word of a frozen collocation ('do'+'so', 'do'+'best', 'dispose'+'of', 'differ'+'from', 'similar'+'to', 'daughter'+'of', 'political'+'will', 'Hudson'+'Bay'). It reads the pair and not the token - the same second token after an unmemorized partner sits at the floor (' so' after do/does/doing 1.0-2.0 vs after say/think/hope/believe 0.0-0.1; ' of' after dispose 1.8 vs after consist/think/talk/approve 0.06-0.18; 'ed' after disjoint 1.95 vs after joint 0.0) and membership is idiosyncratic rather than frequency- or semantics-based ('similar to'/'identical to' fire while 'equal to'/'close to' do not; 'dispose of' fires while 'consist of' does not; 'New York', 'make sure', 'in spite of' and 'part of' are inactive), so label active only the listed pairs, their exact repeats, and further completions of the same split words, and label the opening fragment of a split word (' Con', ' disc', ' dispos', ' disjoint') inactive.

This negative pole fires on a short token that fuses with the token immediately before it into one lexical unit: (i) the particle ' up' after a short, forceful, consonant-final action-verb stem (crack, rack, back, carve, crush, chalk, crank, build, break, patch, shake, shut, hook, mark + up), and (ii) the second, word-internal piece of a word split across tokens (Buch|annon, Phot|acter, arch|ipel, back|g|arden, setProp|ried). It stays at zero after soft/Latinate or vowel-final verbs before the same particle (took/filled/covered/ended/signed/mixed/looked/gave up) and on the same fragment when the word starts at the current token (Cannon, Bacterium), so it tracks the two-token fusion, not the tokens ' up' or the fragments themselves.

This pole reads the word, not the token: it fires when the word being read names a specific structure of the body's skeleton and limbs - named bones and bone adjectives (femur, tibia, fibula, humerus, ulna, patella, carpal, calcaneus, iliac, femoral, tibial), joints and limb regions (hip, knee, elbow, wrist, groin, armpit, thigh, calf, shoulder), skeletal muscles (gastrocnemius, gluteus, sartorius, deltoid) and some English bone compounds (thighbone, shinbone) - peaking 5-13 on the Latin bone names and 1-5 on the rest, with other named organic structures (aorta, pharynx, trachea, rectum, anus, ileum) at 1-3; the peak lands on the word's last fragment, and the identical token 'ula' fires at 8.0 inside 'fibula' but 0.3 inside 'uvula' and 0.1 inside 'nebula'. It stays near its ~0.1 baseline on internal organs and organ adjectives (liver, heart, kidney, cardiac, renal, hepatic, gastric, pulmonary), on generic tissue words (bone, joint, muscle, tendon, cartilage, vertebra), on skin/face parts (skin, eye, tooth, lip), on disease words (arthritis, aneurysm, carcinoma) and on non-body words that share the same final token (humorous, cardiac, special, cubicle), and it is several-fold weaker when the same structure is named in plain English (femur 7.4 vs 'thigh bone' 2.0, patella 4.5 vs 'kneecap' 0.3, iliac 12.9 vs 'hip' 1.5).

L3/N1429- is a token-level template matcher: it fires at the FINAL token of a small set of learned, low-frequency token templates (2-4 BPE tokens long) - technical identifier/API suffixes (',C URLOPT', '.find DOMNode', 'XML StreamReader', '* Factory', 'run_from _argv'), product/font names ('ES Xi', 'Solid Works', 'Semi Bold'), formal labels/names ('About the Publisher', 'World Economic History Congress', 'Hildebrant, Esq.', 'Israeli-Pale stinian', 'Jay anth') and fixed discourse phrases ('That, my', 'Hence, my') - and strength is graded by how much of the template prefix is present (VMware ESXi 2.31 vs ESXi 0.97; About the Publisher 1.34 vs the Publisher 0.04; Using SolidWorks 1.17 vs Using COSMOSWorks 0.12). It is a token-sequence match, not a word, compound, register or memorised-collocation detector: no token fires alone (all 151,936 single-token inputs <= 0.05); high-frequency collocations stay at baseline (New York, United States, Taylor Swift, Microsoft Windows, Joe Biden all <= 0.12); the same word in ordinary running prose stays at baseline (publisher, congress, search, works); the same surface words fail when the context tokenizes them differently (Bernie Sanders reaches 0.87 as Bern+ie+ĠSanders but 0.49-0.54 as ĠBernie+ĠSanders and 0.29 in prose); and changing one template token abolishes it (About the Publisher 1.34 vs About the Editor 0.04; World Economic History Congress 1.15 vs ...Conference 0.05).

N2135+ fires on the punctuation that closes a short label or headline at the start of a text: the colon of a speaker/label tag (line-initial 'Human:' peaks at 15.1, eight times the scan maximum; 'Assistant:' 2.4, 'Q:' 1.8, 'abstract:' 0.8) or the blank line that ends a bare name/headline ('Molly Henderson\n\n' 0.8), and on the line-initial token 'Human' itself (3.5). Ordinary prose, word labels ('Question:', 'User:', 'Note:'), and the same Q:/headline markers once four or more tokens of text precede them stay near zero (<=0.2), while the Human/Assistant tags keep firing at a reduced 4.0/0.9 in later turns.

The pole detects a locative/state predication headed by a preposition or copula: it fires on ' in'/' at'/' on'/' to be' when that word heads a small-clause complement whose subject is the preceding reflexive pronoun ('find/consider/catch/imagine/place/put oneself in X', 'consider oneself to be X'), on that reflexive pronoun itself, and more weakly (1-3.5) on the preposition of the reduced passive 'X is located/situated/positioned in/at Y'. It is a construction detector, not a token detector: ' herself' fires after 'found' (5.5) but not after 'hurt' (0.0), and ' in' fires after 'found herself' (6.4) but not after 'found the dog' (0.4) or after an event-locative adjunct ('hurt herself in the kitchen', 0.1); a weak separate tail fires on digit continuations of alphanumeric tokens ('P4'+'5', 'sha3'+'8', ~2.0).

This pole is a ' with'-token detector: it peaks on the token ' with' itself (nearly all of its activations above 1.0 are on ' with'; no other token family comes close), but only when the left context makes that 'with' a descriptive/attributive connector to a thing rather than a complement - i.e. when ' with' is immediately preceded (i) by a comma ('the engines, with each cylinder firing', 'the paper, with co-authors in Boston') or (ii) by an indefinite thing noun phrase 'a/an (adj) N' ('a loan with a high interest rate', 'an old bridge with a stone arch', 'a phone with a cracked screen'). It stays at baseline when 'with' is a verb/adjective complement or part of a fixed multiword preposition ('filled with', 'compatible with', 'along with', 'together with', 'dealt with'), when it follows a definite person, group, event or relational noun or a definite object NP without a comma ('the man with a beard', 'the team with the best record', 'a chat with a friend', 'the problem with the plan', 'the car with the flat tyre'), and in clause-initial 'With ...' ('With a loud crash, the door fell'); the same neuron's positive pole is instead a broad ' into' detector.

This pole fires on the head (second) word of a two-word noun compound: a common noun used attributively immediately followed by the noun it classifies or supplies the argument for ('price tag', 'culture clash', 'system partition', 'information sharing', 'bank failures', 'house visits'). The same head word goes near-silent when it follows a determiner, numeral, adjective or participle ('the tag', 'big tag', 'quick partition', 'swimming pool') or when it comes first ('tag price'), the modifier noun itself never fires, and strength is largest for abstract/event/relational heads (clash, swap, change, war, decision, failure, visit, gap) and weak for concrete object compounds (coffee cup, car door).

Fires on the word 'official' used as an adjective or adverb meaning formally sanctioned or authorised status ('official trailer/website/figures/capacity', 'officially announced', 'now official'), and on its cognates in other languages (French officiel(lement), German offiziell, Spanish oficial(mente)), peaking on the token that completes the 'offic-' stem (e.g. 'iel', 'izi', 'ical'), at about 0.55-0.9 of max. It is much weaker (about 0.15-0.35 of max) for the noun sense 'a government official' / 'officials' and for near-synonyms 'unofficial', 'formally', 'formal', 'authorized'. It is essentially silent on 'office', 'officer', other status adjectives ('state', 'verified', 'personal', 'final'), and on the very first token of a text.

The positive pole is a right-edge detector for a lexicalized multi-token designation: it peaks on the token that completes a fixed term, abbreviation, proper name or idiom rather than on any word - ' service' closing 'quality of service' (2.5-5.9), ' life' closing 'quality of life' (3.2) and 'end of life' (4.0), ' birth' closing 'date of birth' (5.8) and 'place of birth' (0.9-2.1), ' death' closing 'cause of death' (1.4), ' Service' closing 'terms of service' (3.0), ' sale' closing 'point of sale' (4.5), ' day' closing 'time of day' (4.8), 'F' closing DOF (3.4-4.9), 'B' closing DOB (2.8), 'V' closing POV (4.1), 'A' closing COA (3.1), ' Boh' closing 'Niels Bohr' (1.9), ' in' closing 'join in' (2.3), ' down' closing 'stopping down' (2.3), and the 'of' that closes a fixed prepositional frame such as 'at the time of' (2.7) or 'in event of' (3.1); the word alone is neither necessary nor sufficient, because the scan's other 17 occurrences of ' service' read 0.00-0.47, ' birth' reads 0.00 in 'assigned at birth', ' death' 0.00-0.67 in 'rate/perinatal/sudden/cell death', ' view' 0.00-0.16 outside 'point of view', and every ' day' in the scan is at most 0.11 ('the end of the day', 'the next day'), while breaking the unit collapses the peak. Breaking the designation kills it on the same words: inserting a determiner ('quality of the service' 0.09 vs 2.50, 'terms of the service' 0.11 vs 2.99, 'cause of the death' 0.22 vs 0.98, 'quality of the life' 0.66 vs 3.18), reordering the compound ('service quality' 0.10 vs 2.50), spelling out an abbreviation ('depth of field' 0.21 vs DOF 3.39, 'Enter date here' 0.11 vs 'Enter DOB here' 2.83), or swapping the name ('Niels Borh' 0.23 vs 1.87, 'Tour de Suisse' 0.09 vs 'Tour de France' 0.40, 'DOG'/'POT'/'COX' 0.07-0.26 vs DOF/POV/COA) - while an unrelated substitution ('hospitals' for 'clinics') leaves it at 2.50 vs 2.50; leftovers outside the claim: membership of the unit list is lexical rather than semantic ('quality of care' 0.28, 'bill of materials' 0.10, 'standard of living' 0.14 stay at the floor although near-synonyms fire), and the mechanism is retrospective (zero-ablating the pole moves next-token KL by at most 1e-2 with no coherent promoted token set; Jacobian kurtosis 3.6, lens agreement 0), with the negative pole peaking on fragments of unfamiliar strings (' hp' in 'Jodhpur', ' imers' in 'heterodimers', ' led' in Norwegian 'ledes'), the un-assembled complement of this right-edge feature.

The positive pole is a retrospective detector for the head word of a hedged scalar relation - the preposition, particle, comparative or small-amount noun that states how far something sits from a reference point - and it fires strongly only when that word is immediately preceded by a small-degree downtoner: 'just under/over/past/before/after/outside/inside/beyond/above/below/behind/ahead/up/off/short of/shy of/left of/right of/south of', 'a little more/less/lower', 'slightly off/below', 'a bit behind', 'shortly before', 'a small/slight/tiny chance', 'a little bit/something' (measured peaks 4.5-14.3, e.g. 'just under' 13.6 and 'a little more' 6.5 against 'under' 1.2 and 'more' 0.0 with no left modifier). The same relational head after an intensifier instead of a downtoner ('very', 'well', 'much', 'a lot', 'far'), after a non-small approximator ('about', 'almost', 'nearly', 'roughly', 'exactly'), with no left modifier, or after the same downtoner in front of an ordinary noun ('a little dog/cake/water') stays at 0.0-3.1, and 'just' plus a non-relational word ('just the/a/want/like/because/thinking') is inert, while a preceding measure phrase ('nine miles east of', 'three hours after', 'two feet under') gives the same head-word peak at a weaker 1.5-3.8 and colon clock times ('3:05', '1:31', '2:03') are a further weaker offshoot (2.5-6.3 on the last digit, with plain numbers like '199'/'305'/'1990' silent).

L3/N4398- is a stored-token-string (n-gram) detector rather than a token detector: it fires at the current token when the token immediately before it - sometimes the two before - matches the first half of a memorised two- or three-token string, i.e. the joint inside a rare word ('out' in Maci Book|out 2.74, 'ot' in Disc|otek 1.68, 'ond' in Rosam|ond 1.16, 'im' in poly|imide 1.51, 'ort' in Skv|ort|zov 1.34, 'C' in CAM|C 1.65, '8' in sha3|84 0.77) or the second word of a stored collocation, proper name, product name or technical term (' Out' in The Great| Outdoors 5.04, ' Public' in GNU General| Public 2.10, ' Natural' in Department of| Natural 1.39, ' league' in major| league 1.51, ' account' after social 1.23, ' acid' after metabolic 1.05, ' tape' after police 0.94, ' Pictures' after Universal 0.76). The string, not the token id, carries the feature: the same token is at baseline under any other predecessor (' Public' 1.78 after 'General' vs 0.02 after 'the'; ' league' 1.51 after 'major' vs <0.19 after 'youth'; ' Out' 5.04 after 'Great' vs 1.18 after 'Big'), other continuations of the same prefix do not fire (GNU General| Assembly 0.02, Department of| History 0.00, Universal| Studios 0.01, police| car 0.06), strength is graded by how much of the stored prefix is present (GNU General| Public 2.10 > General| Public 1.78 > the| Public 0.02; Department of| Natural 1.39 > Office of| Natural 0.93 > Bureau of| Natural <0.30), and the mechanism is retrospective: strength is fixed by the left context alone (2.102 with either 'License' or 'Licence' after the trigger; 0.792 for ' de' with either 'Ville' or 'Crillon' after it; the unspaced retokenisation 'Great'+'Outdoors' still fires at 4.88), the Jacobian lens is flat (kurtosis 3.3, 0% overlap with the logit lens) and zero-ablating the pole leaves the strongest continuations (' Public' after GNU General, ' Natural' after Department of) unchanged.

The negative pole tracks stative, non-agentive predication: it peaks on base-form copula and stative predicates (' be', ' have', ' need', ' depend', ' require', ' resemble', ' equal', ' mean', ' include', ' involve', ' seem', ' appear', ' weigh') and on relational nominalisations such as 'variability', 'prevalence', 'incidence', 'similarity', 'correlation' together with the preposition that introduces their complement (' of', ' between', ' with', ' for'). It falls to near zero when the same slot holds an agentive/eventive verb ('build', 'destroy', 'attack', 'give', 'make'), when the clause subject is an agentive human ('They', 'She', 'The authors') rather than impersonal 'It'/'This', and on concrete nouns in the identical frame ('the box of the table' = 0.03 vs 'the variability of the system' = 1.10).

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a conventionalized local frame opened by preceding material: a comma closing a fronted adjunct ('far away, there lived') or a list-final item before its conjunction ('one egg, and'), or a complement selected by its head ('Once'+'upon', 'sat'+'on', 'import numpy'+'as', 'through'+weekday, 'ORDER BY'+column). Peak strength is set jointly by the head-plus-peak combination rather than either token alone, so swapping the head ('sat'->'waited') or the peak (','->'and'/'plus', 'upon'->'atop', weekday->'xyz') collapses firing while same-frame substitutions (Sunday->Monday) leave it unchanged.

Retrospective detector for an approximate (vague, small) amount phrase: the pole peaks on the vague-quantity head of "a little X", "a few X", "a bit of X" or "a couple of X" -- most strongly on ' little' and on the ' of' that follows ' bit' or ' couple' -- and it tracks the construction rather than the word, since ' little' stays quiet as a size adjective ("the little girl", 0.37), in the negative-polarity idiom ("Little did he know", 0.00) and as a bare quantifier ("little hope", 0.12; "Few people", 0.09). Exact and large quantity words do not fire it ("a lot of" 0.14-0.49, "a piece of" 0.48, "a number of" 0.04, "a dozen" 0.23, "several" 0.00, "many" 0.13, "plenty of" 0.10) and neither do exact numerals ("45 minutes" 0.12, "in 2017" 0.17); every strong (>0.5) activation is in the SwiGLU g+u- regime (the diffuse <=0.5 g-u+ response to ordinary content words is a separate broadcast regime), and these leftovers are outside the claim: determiners and quantifiers right after light verbs ("could use a" 2.85, "learns a" 2.71, "take some time" 1.99, "snap a few" 1.83), the word-piece 'm' in identifiers ("dbmigrate", 4.35), measure nouns such as ' seconds' ("a few seconds" 3.10, which fire even after 'several' and are themselves top token-identity drivers), and numerals in approximative frames ("an hour or two" 2.34, "or three" 2.25).

The positive pole fires on the token that completes a gendered civilian title of address (Mr, Ms, Mrs, Miss, Mister, Madam, Mme, Monsieur; more weakly Madame, Herr, Señor), peaking on the abbreviation period of 'Mr.'/'Ms.'/'Mrs.' (~9-12) or on the title token itself when no period follows (~7-9), whether or not a personal name follows ('Mr. Coffee', 'Mr. Universe', 'Thank you, Mr. President'). Professional or noble titles (Dr ~2.5, Prof ~1, Sir ~1), other abbreviation periods ('p.m.', 'U.S.', 'St.') and bare names stay near zero; its Jacobian-lens output promotes the same title tokens (' Mr', '先生'), so it is a retrospective 'Mister/Missus title just read' detector rather than a predictor of the upcoming surname.

The negative pole (weak; max ~2.3) fires on the completing piece of a small set of memorised multi-token terms: compass-direction compounds ending '-Central' (North-/West-/South-Central, 1.1-2.2), Django '{% csrf' (1.5-2.5), front-end class/directive idioms ('form-control', 'ng-controller', 'btn-primary', 0.6-1.7) and a few code identifiers ('ImproperlyConfigured', 'MultivaluedMap', 'BOOST_MPL_AUX', SQL 'NOT NULL', ~1.0-1.5), plus descriptive-word + College/University names ('Imperial College', "King's College", 'Free University', 'Central University', 0.6-1.4). The same continuation tokens stay below threshold after a plain proper noun or in ordinary prose (Boston/Harvard/Royal College, Open/National University, self-control in a sentence, 'central district', 'config file', 'Central Park'), so it is a retrospective, lexically narrow 'fixed compound just completed' detector rather than a general subword-continuation detector; its Jacobian-lens output is diffuse (kurtosis 3.4) and it suppresses the ' Mr'/'先生' tokens its positive pole promotes.

The negative pole fires on a relative pronoun at the moment it opens a relative clause: a definite D-word or wh-pronoun (German der/die/das/den/dem/denen, Danish-Norwegian der/den/det/de/dem, Dutch die, English which/whose/whom, Spanish (el/lo) cual, French dont/qui) sitting in the clause-linking slot immediately after a comma or a preposition, where it refers back to an antecedent (peak 2.3-5.7 there). The same form as a determiner after a verb or at a sentence start, or as an interrogative, demonstrative, indefinite article or non-D-word marker, stays near zero: 'Ich sehe den Mann' 0.0 and 'Ich gebe dem Mann das Buch' 0.0 on the D-word, 'de partij' 0.07, 'Die Frau steht dort' 0.04, 'Which book did you read last year?' peaks 0.20, '¿Cuál es tu respuesta?' 0.70, 'Qui a fait cela?' 0.26, 'dieser' 0.37 even after a comma, English 'that' 0.0 after a comma, 'dass/weil/because' 0.05-0.32; because the decision is made at the pronoun itself, a comma followed by an article in a German list ('Der Hund, die Katze...' 3.48) is a predicted false positive, as the disambiguating noun has not been read yet.

This pole fires at a delimiter (a newline, a period/colon/semicolon/comma-plus-newline, or a closing brace) that ends one element of a multi-element parallel enumeration — repeated same-format lines or entries such as configure-flag lists, bibliography or roster entries, numbered headings, or repeated declarations and boilerplate paragraphs — with same-format material continuing after it; the same delimiter ending an isolated sentence or a single item leaves it quiet.

The pole fires on a token that names a marked degree of something's worth, adequacy or capability - the deficiency/incapacity family (inferior, worthless and worthlessness, helpless(ness), powerless, hopeless(ness), incompetent and incompetence, incapable, inadequate, ineffective, insignificant, negligible, imperfect and imperfection, futile, failure, weakness(es), defective, disposable, blame/blaming) and the eminence family (perfection, superior and superiority, excellence, greatness, mastery, dignity, precious, worth, worthy, unworthy, merit) - and is graded by what is being graded: strongest when the word grades a person or a person's act ('He felt worthless' 1.65x the scan max, 'He was worthless' 0.93x) and weaker, though still above the active threshold, when it grades an object or is used in a non-evaluative sense ('the inferior vena cava' 0.58x, 'Superior Court' 0.36x, 'This product is inferior' 0.79x); the same words in other languages (inférieur, supérieur, inferiore, wertlos) stay near zero, as do their abstract nominal forms only when the stem is not a worth stem (darkness, sadness, kindness, fairness, rudeness). It stays at the floor (under 0.05x max) for everyday quality adjectives and for other dimensions - good, great, excellent, superb, outstanding, bad, poor, nice, fine; magnitude: important, significant, substantial, crucial, essential, major; raw potency: strong, powerful, weak, dominant; money: price, cost, rich, wealthy, expensive; social rank and honour: rank, status, prestige, respect, honour, fame, shame; emotion: angry, sad, happy, afraid; aesthetics: beautiful, ugly - so it is not an evaluation, valence, frequency or abstract-noun-suffix detector.

The pole fires on the joint token of a locally-fixed construction: the token at which a familiar template hands over to its fillable part. It peaks on the ' in'/' of' keyword after a 'for (var/let x' header (and on the 'in' membership operator, 'if (x in y)'), on the connector right after a quoted string argument of a DSL call ('describe "..." do'), on the first token of a quoted attribute value just after '=\"', on an attribute name that follows a closing quote inside a tag ('\" xmlns', '\" id', '\" width'), and on ' in' after a defect noun (hole, gap, mistake, error); it stays near zero on the fixed prefix before that joint, on the filler tokens that follow it, and throughout ordinary prose, where the same words (' in' after cat, book, wall, code) do not fire.

Fires on a sub-word token that ends exactly at a Greek/Latin combining-form prefix, linking vowel included, when the token is a bare prefix waiting for its stem or used on its own: 'micro'/' micro'/' Micro' strongest (~0.8-1.0 of max, e.g. ' micro|flora', 'micro|seconds', 'a new micro'), then 'tetra' ('tet|ra'), 'angio' ('ang|io'), 'icosa' ('icos|ah'), 'andro' ('And|ro'), 'xylo' ('xy|lo'), 'polyc', ' macro' (~0.5-0.9), and weaker for ' nano', ' mega', ' mono', ' poly', ' multi', ' mill', ' hex', ' hydro' (~0.25-0.5). It stays near zero on whole-word tokens that only contain such a prefix (' microwave', ' microscopic', ' microtime', ' nanoparticles', ' psychology'), on fragments cut before the linking vowel (' angi', ' cy', ' tri', ' di'), on ordinary words, and at the first token of a sequence. The context before the token barely matters.

Detects the letter c/C when it names the C programming language family, retrospectively. The strongest case (8-18) is the lowercase 'c' inside a copyright mark '(c)' right after 'Copyright'/'COPYRIGHT'/'Licensed', as in source-file license headers; uppercase '(C)' is much weaker (2-4) and '(x)', '(b)', a bare '©' or '(c)' with no Copyright word stay near 0. Moderate activity (3-8) comes when ' C' names the language (in C, ANSI C, C++, C#, C/C++, Objective-C, the C:\ drive) or on the token that disambiguates an earlier ' C' as the language (' language'/' programming' after ' C'), and on C-ecosystem tokens ('.h' in #include <...h>, malloc, free, printf). The letter C used non-programmatically (vitamin C, grade C) and other language names (Python, Java, R, D, F#, CUDA) stay near 0.

Fires on a prefix (unary) operator token that opens an operand where the syntax expects an operand, not an operator, in code or arithmetic: above all a space-preceded unary minus ' -' right after a binary/comparison/logical operator, '=', ':=', ',', 'return' or a keyword ('5 - -3', '3 + -5', '&& -y', 'i == -1', 'foo(a, -1)', 'return -1'), strongest (~3-5.7) when the preceding token is itself an operator. Other operand-opening prefixes are weaker (unary ' +' ~2.5, ' ~'/' !' ~1-1.5, a regex-literal '/', an ObjC message ' [' in code), while the same ' -' used as a binary operator after an operand ('x - 1', '5 - 3', '3 - 2' in prose) and literals without a sign stay near zero.

Retrospective, and the weak side of a two-lobed neuron: the sharp negative pole is a firearms/hunting detector ('hunting' 7.8, 'cartridge' 8.0, 'rifle' 5.9), while the positive pole fires on tokens that carry technical notation or technical naming rather than narrative content - LaTeX math delimiters and closers ('$$', '}}', '}' followed by '\', ';' glued to a closing '$'), markup and identifier syntax ('@android:', '<name', '_name', '("'), and the second element of technical compound terms ('orthogonal', 'beam splitter'). Plain narrative prose, and any firearms/hunting text, stays at the floor (peak below 0.35 of max).

Fires on the word that names an industrial production site or sector: the head noun or adjective of 'factory/plant/mill/works/refinery/quarry/mine/industry/industrial/manufacturing/processor/blue-collar', strongest when the preceding modifier names a heavy-industry or commodity good (steel, cotton, sugar, garment, poultry processing, iron), as in 'steel industry', 'sugar mill', 'processing plant', 'Iron Works', 'industrial revolution'. It stays weak (<~25% of max) when the same word has a non-industrial sense (potted/flowering plant, pepper mill, complete works) or names a service sector (insurance, music, banking industry), and on generic production verbs like 'making'. It reacts to what has been read (retrospective) and does not prepare a specific next token.

The pole fires on the second, head part of a technical term written as one fused word: the object noun that closes a verb+object identifier (Set|Key, Load|Library, add|Class, set|RequestHeader, clear|Cache, add_library, import_module, To|Primitive, Start|Activity) and the stem of a fused prefixed technical word (de|ferences, anti|-western, Pan|-European, hypo|glyc|emic). It peaks when the two parts are written with no space between them and is usually well below the activity line (though not always zero) when a space separates them, while the same nouns as ordinary vocabulary ('the key is on the table', 'the service was slow'), noun-first or possessive compounds (camelCase, myKey, documentParser, ClassName, whiteSpace) and nonce strings (florbulateCache, SetBanana, camelKey) stay near zero.

This pole fires retrospectively on two triggers: (a) digit tokens inside a four-digit number read as a calendar year, peaking on an early digit (e.g. the '9' in 'In 1969', the '8' in 'the year 1847'), strongest for plausible Western years and silent on identical digits in counts ('count 1847/1969'), quantities ('11 cats', '500 mg', '13 billion') or implausible years ('7351', '4823'); (b) the word-form ' museum' in any context ('The museum', 'toured the museum'), staying silent on near-synonym building nouns (library, gallery, monument, artifact, prison).

Fires retrospectively on a noun or verb token that reports or assigns a position on an ordered evaluative or measurement scale — school, medical, product-condition, sports, or slope grades, ranks, scores, indices, acuity levels, or equivalents — with peak strength on explicit grade/rank tokens used in a classification or measurement frame.

The negative pole fires on the token that completes a stative, generic or passive predicate about an abstract, non-physical subject (a task, question, decision, action, problem, work, rule, price or quantity), typically built from a high-frequency general-purpose verb - do, make, take, answer, solve, apply, occur, happen, rise, be true, be forthcoming - as in 'no action was taken', 'little progress was made', 'the work is done', 'the question was answered', 'the problem was solved', 'no explanation was forthcoming', 'this is true of the iron cross', 'the same rules apply to everyone'. It stays near zero when the same predicate word takes a physical object or a specific event as subject ('the phone was answered', 'the dishes were done', 'the house was sold'), when the clause is active or agentive ('they took no action', 'he answered all the questions'), or when a lexically specific verb replaces the general one ('the work was sold', 'the decision was announced', 'the matter was resolved').

L4/N3740- fires on the token that closes a memorised multi-word frame: the fixed second element of a stock phrase or template whose identity is pinned by the preceding anchor word, not by the sentence. The strongest frames are conventional gender binomials ('him or her' 3.0, 'his or her' 2.6-3.1, 'men and women' 1.5-1.9, 'mothers and fathers' 1.5), then grammatical stock phrases ('so as to' 1.2-1.7, 'able to' 0.9-1.0, 'the fact that' 1.1, 'whether or not' 0.6, 'on the other hand' 0.7, 'once again' 1.9, 'in their own right' 1.8) and code/markup templates ('@+id' 1.7, '$_SESSION' 0.7-1.1, '<?xml', '____' 1.7); it is not a predictability, frequency or coordination detector, since equally probable continuations outside a memorised frame ('wanted to' 0.00, 'ready to' 0.07, 'yes or no' 0.13, 'own hands' 0.32, 'once more' 0.18) stay near zero and a merely conventional-but-specific pairing ('king and queen' 0.21) never reaches the collective-pair level.

The negative pole fires on a closed family of formal, Latin-derived process and planning words - 'consider / consideration / considering', 'research', 'study', 'explore', 'improve', 'seek', 'mitigate', 'feasible', 'sufficient', 'assessment', 'analysis', ' per capita', 'red tourism', and the fixed phrases 'Did you know' and 'not only ... but also' - and on the function words (' of', ' that') that continue those phrases, but only when the word sits in the hedged, deliberative frame of written expository prose: after a deontic or necessity marker (should, ought to, must, need to, have to, 'recommend that you', 'it is important to'), after 'worth', after source-introducing 'According to', or inside those fixed constructions. It stays silent on the same words as the plain finite predicate of a simple declarative ('we consider the options', 'I know the answer', 'we study / we explore the proposal'), when 'will' replaces a deontic modal, when a near-synonym outside the family is used ('should examine / assess / evaluate / review'), and in casual narrative text; its opposite pole instead fires on policy-action and goal vocabulary (phase out, eradicate, fight against, campaign, priority), and every top negative peak is in the same g+u- SwiGLU regime, so this is one job, not two.
