Fires on the first sub-word piece of a multi-token surname or place name: a short capitalised fragment, mostly W-initial (' We', ' Wo', ' Wa', ' W') and also ' Ra', ' Ke', ' Ka', ' Kl', 'ke', ' dela', that sits in a name slot (after a first name, a title such as Mr./Dr., or 'at'/'in' before an institution or place), so the word is still unfinished (Weisberg, Weill, Inverkeithing, Raanan). It stays silent on the same letters as a complete word (the pronoun 'We' at a clause start, single-token names such as Weber, Goldberg, Johnson, Inverness), on later pieces of the name ('ill', 'isberg'), and on other first pieces such as ' Gins', ' Br' or ' St'. A weaker offshoot fires on a pivot token inside memorised boilerplate, e.g. ' via' in a 'Sun-Sentinel via AP' photo credit and '=' in 'initial-scale=1'.

The negative pole is a licensing/copyright-notice detector: it fires on the standard notice that names who holds a document's copyright and states the terms under which it may be used ('Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License")', 'Permission is hereby granted, free of charge...', 'This program is free software... GNU General Public License', 'All rights reserved', MIT/GPL/Apache/CC-BY header blocks), most strongly when such a multi-line notice heads a source file, and more weakly on other verbatim standard strings of the same files (e.g. the canonical Go 'if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }' check, fixed log/error formats, CDN URLs and version strings). It keys on the stock wording of that notice register rather than on legal meaning: the same licence terms paraphrased in fresh prose, and other legal registers (contracts, EULAs, statutes, court opinions, patent claims), stay near zero, so predict active on licence/copyright notice text in any language and inactive on ordinary prose and on legal prose that is not a licence notice.

The negative pole fires on the token that completes the stem of a Latin/Romance word the text is still writing, i.e. the piece on which the word in progress stops being stem material and only an ending can follow ('iter-' in iteración, ' administr-' in administrating, 'eler-' in decelerations, 'ug-' in centrifugation, ' demand-' in French demandent, 'cancel-' in Portuguese cancelou, 'ibr-' in calibrating); it is silent on earlier pieces of the same word while the stem is still incomplete (' centrif' before '-ug-', 'dec' before '-eler-', ' contr' before '-ari-'), on the same strings when they end a complete word ('demand' in 'The union will demand safer conditions', 'inform' in 'Please inform the committee', 'reconsider' in 'We should reconsider the plan'), on whole words that arrive in one token ('iteration', 'administration', 'centrifuge') and on non-Latinate fragments ('fenugreek'). It is retrospective, not lookahead: the peak is fixed by the prefix alone (the same ' demand' piece reads 10.79 after a French prefix and 0.03 after an English one, and deleting the ending after 'reconsider' leaves its 6.33 unchanged), and zero-ablating the pole spreads a small loss over the whole ending family (aggregate KL 2.1e-03, shifted tokens 'at', 'ation', 'ating', 'ar', 'ados', 'atively', concentration below the 0.5 gate) instead of concentrating it on one upcoming token.

L18/N2906- fires where a subject gets back to a state, place or role it held before: it peaks on the return verb or on the possessive/determiner that follows it in spans such as 'went back to her usual routine', 'regained their previous level', 'reverted to his old habits', 'reclaimed its place', 'returned to action', 'took over the position from his predecessor' and 'replacing collagen lost by the natural aging process', and sits at its floor for forward or novel change ('reached their highest level', 'moved to the top of the league'), for bare repetition ('played the same song again', 'reread the letter twice'), for plain possession ('picked up his coat') and for neutral prose. Its weight rows encode the same concept (gate 恢复/重建/修复/重返/recover/lost, up repar/repl/补/rebuild, down 重新/replacement/rebuilt), opposite to the positive pole, which fires on privation and removal ('the losses were serious', 'the storm broke the windows', 'the parts were removed'); isolated single-token spikes on word pieces like 'ash' in rare surnames or ' (' before an abbreviation are a separate, weaker token-identity component.

Fires at the slot where a numeric value is about to be given for a measured attribute that has already been named (age, weight, size, dilation, percentage, warranty length, an Android layout_width/height): the bare space token ' ' before the digits, the '="' after a dimension attribute, or a connective right after such a number that opens a second bound or an approximation (' or', ' to', ' and', ' about': '16 years or more', 'age from 15 to 99', '70 kg or so', '70-80 mesh and smaller'). It stays weak (< 0.25 of max) when the same number or connective appears without a quantity attribute named before it (e.g. 'range in name from 15 to 99', 'was named and found to be 1.8', 'layout_title="', 'smoke or drink'); a minority of top examples on non-numeric words (' videos', ' insured', 'isha') are not covered.

The pole fires on four specific slots, peaking on that token: (1) the preposition that introduces the weapon or instrument in a scene of violence or crime, set by the scene rather than the verb ('attacked his wife with a screwdriver', 'the gunman met the guard with a rifle', also 'using', and cross-lingually only here: French 'avec' and Spanish 'con' in 'atacó ... con un cuchillo'; about 2.5-4); (2) attributive 'due' and the degree adjective of a manner 'with' phrase ('due process/diligence/respect', 'with great care/confidence', including sentence-initial 'With great care,'; about 2.4-4.7, while clause-final 'due to' is weaker at about 1.1-1.6); (3) a year digit, usually the last, in copyright notices and parenthesised birth-death dates ('Copyright (c) 2016', '(5 July 1914 - 11 April 2009)'; about 1.4-3.1); and (4) more weakly (about 1.0-2.3), has/have right after a chemical, drug, molecule or theory subject that states its property or effect ('the drug has no effect', 'the compound has a melting point'). It is inactive (below about 0.9) on years in running prose ('built in 1940', 'In July 1914'), predicative 'is due', non-violent tool use and comitative, noun-modifying or lexicalised with/avec ('fixed the shelf with', 'helped his wife with', 'the girl with the red hat', 'agree with', 'diagnosed with', 'La chambre avec balcon'), sentence-initial possessive 'With three assistants...', possession HAVE with an ordinary subject (person, organisation, place or building: 'the hotel/museum/committee has', French 'Le musee a une collection', 'I/we/you have'), and modal 'have to', where 'have' and 'to' stay below 0.5 (the one known leftover is 'Visitors have to show a badge', at 1.4 on 'show').

The pole fires on the indefinite determiner 'some' (and much more weakly on 'any') where it is used as a hedge that leaves the amount, degree or kind of something unspecified - the reading of 'need some help', 'for some time', 'some form of debt', 'some kind of', 'is there some way', 'showed some interest' - and its write at that position is the matching vague-classifier set ('kind', 'sort', 'type', 'form', 'way', 'time') instead of the specific noun the model would otherwise name. It stays at floor on the very same token where 'some' merely picks out particular countable individuals that are met, bought, seen or counted ('I met some friends', 'I bought some books', 'in some cases', 'for some reason'), on a sentence-initial 'Some' with nothing before it, on every other quantifier (several, many, few, a few, certain), and on compounds (someone, something, somewhat, somehow); and because the peak is on the determiner itself only the text before it can matter, so changing the word after 'some' never changes the value.

This pole fires retrospectively on the first chunk of a fixed multi-token expression, a lexicalized compound (sun|spots, space|walks, leather|backs, pain|killers), a fixed title or name (Moon|Patrol), or a set collocation (buzz|word, Down|fall), when preceding context primes that exact expression: repeated prior mentions boost it strongly and a constraining frame suffices with no repetition. It is near-silent on the completion chunk itself and on the same word used outside any fixed expression, so its peak always lands just before the predictable continuation rather than on it.

Fires retrospectively on the digits of a year (its first one or two digits, e.g. the '1' and '0' of 1087), or of a century ordinal ('12th'), when the numeral dates a past event or entity in a historical, ecclesiastical or encyclopedic sentence: a temporal phrase attached to a historical subject ('the abbey was built/founded in 1087' 23.4, 'the king died in 1087 at Rouen' 19.4, 'from 1087 to 1100' 22.9, 'the abbey grew in the 12th century' 17.3 of a 23.1 scale), where older years fire higher than modern ones (1087 ~23, 2019 ~14) and a modern or commercial subject fires much less (the company was founded in 1087 ~12, the website was built in 1087 ~0.3). It stays near zero (0.2-2) on the same numerals as quantities, counts, page or room numbers or bare subjects ('the abbey housed 1087 monks', 'the price was 1087 dollars', '1087 was a good year for the abbey'), when the year is fronted to the sentence start with no historical context before it ('In 1087 the abbey was finished' alone 2.2, but 19.3 after 'The monks were devout.'), and on brackets in code, except a secondary mode on the bracket opening a shell test after a conditional keyword ('if [', 'while [', ' [[' fires 12-18 while 'if (' and ordinary brackets stay near zero).

Retrospective: the pole's strong canonical-regime (g+u+) response fires on a noun token that names a channel, bond, agreement, proof, or barrier through which two other things relate (river, bridge, link, treaty, theorem, equation, inequality), graded by how directly the noun denotes such a link (river/treaty/bridge/theorem high; mountain/dog/guess/novel/rumor near zero in identical frames). The weak broad firing on surrounding glue words (prepositions, articles, spaces before numbers, verbs like proved) comes from a separate SwiGLU double-negative (g-u-) background process, and the pole predicts no specific next token (none of the tokens after peaks overlap its connect/separate/linking lens list).

This pole fires on the very first token of the input when that token is a structural function word or code keyword that opens an incomplete multi-token structure (articles, demonstratives, prepositions, subordinators, conjunctions, interrogatives, auxiliaries, or statement keywords such as import/from/def); it stays silent when the input opens with a content word (proper/common nouns, lexical verbs, interjections, discourse adverbs) and when the same structural tokens appear anywhere past absolute position 0.

Retrospective: in its main (g+u+) regime the pole fires on a content token that fills a delimited structural slot — prototypically a table cell right after a ' | ' delimiter (strength 1-4, abolished to ~0 when the pipe is swapped for 'and'/',' at equal token length), and also tag-enclosed, parenthesized, or SQL BY-clause/statement-final content, with extra boost for column-header-like words (name/email/col). Its output direction specifically promotes ' | '-family pipe tokens (Jacobian kurtosis 7.7, z>10), pushing continuations toward pipe-delimited structure. A separate weak SwiGLU double-negative (g-u-) regime fires ~0.3 on common function words ('on','to','the'), explaining the scan's low prose tail and the 59% token-identity variance rather than the strong peaks.

The negative pole fires when the current token is a word-initial subword fragment — the first piece of a longer word that the tokenizer split into several tokens — with a learned per-fragment gain that is large for p-/re- technical-vocabulary onsets (' pem' in pemphigus, ' pe' in peptidase, ' p' in pumice or penguin, ' per' in percutaneous, ' rep'/'rem'/'ref') and small for most other fragments (' ps', ' pl', ' pr', ' punct'); pieces after the first ('ph', 'ig', 'ands') are much weaker. It is near zero for ordinary complete words (even rare or p-initial ones: patients, people, pneumonia, granite) and for nonsense fragments, weakens when the same word already appeared in the context, and also fires on pieces of non-word strings — DOI digit runs after a citation cue, page references ('p. 2'), p-values ('p = .05'), 'P.3d' citations, 'per cent', hyphenated compounds ('air-powder').

The pole is a 'cool, dry, shaded, sheltered spot' feature of natural-language prose: it fires on the token where the model commits to a place phrase - the article or condition adjective of 'in/on a ___ place/room/spot' (' a', ' cool', ' moist', ' shady') or the preposition/verb that opens the locative complement ('in', 'under', 'out', 'to', 'seek', 'seeking') - when the clause says where an entity is, is put, is kept or takes itself, and it peaks hardest on the preservation idiom 'keep/store it in a cool[, dry/dark] place' (base activations 19-26, above the scan's 17.5 maximum) and on animals choosing a sheltered or shady spot ('seek shelter' 16.9, 'retreat to lower levels' 12.5, 'a shady spot' 13.7, 'moist areas under vegetation' 9.7, 'a window out of direct sunlight' 10.9). It is retrospective, not a token detector and not lookahead: its output direction promotes exactly this input vocabulary (凉 cool, 遮 shade, 干燥 dry, 通风 ventilated, 晴 clear, shaded, shelter, away) and zero-ablating it removes probability from cool/dry/place/shelter/away without concentrating on a single next token, while the same words outside a place phrase ('a cool breeze' 2.6, 'a cool drink' 2.1, cool meaning stylish 0.1, 'the cake stays moist' 0.1, 'I seek your advice' 0.1) and unqualified or incidental locations ('the keys are in a small drawer' 0.7, 'the contract is in a brown envelope' 0.1) stay near the floor; its opposite pole is the machine-literal pole of the same neuron (IP/port digits, URL path pieces, partial UTF-8 bytes), so the two poles split machine-formatted literals from prose about places and their conditions (peaks on hydration and protective-clothing advice are leftovers this account does not cover).

L19/N1638- fires wherever the text names the source being cited in a report - a person or their role, an organisation's mouthpiece, or a document/study/report - at the point that phrase is the subject of the clause: it builds across the phrase as the phrase is specified ('a spokesman' 4.0 -> 'a spokesman for the group' 9.5, 13.5 in the scan's top snippet) and peaks on the phrase's last token, immediately before the reporting verb ('..., a source' 8.1, '..., he' 8.0, 'police officials' 6.1, 'the project's team leader' 6.9, 'a CIBC study from earlier this year' 6.4, 'the report' 7.6), most strongly in the postposed attribution tag after quoted or reported speech. It is near zero on the same words in any other role - as an object ('We fired a spokesman for the group' 0.5, 'We questioned a CIBC study from earlier this year' 0.1, 'We called Smith about the deal' 0.1), as a bare name or title subject of an ordinary sentence ('Smith said the deal was done' 0.4 over the whole prompt, 'The senator said the deal was done' 0.4, 'After the meeting, Smith said the deal was done' 0.4, all below the 3.4 active threshold) - and on the reporting verb itself (' said' is 0.0 at every peak); its output direction does promote exactly that verb family (' said'/' says'/' told', Jacobian z 12.2, kurtosis 5.5) and it lifts P(' said') when intact (0.288 vs 0.231 ablated on 'a spokesman for the group'), but the protocol's lookahead probe returns retrospective (concentration 0.40 < 0.5, KL ~1e-3) because the write is spread across the family, so this is recorded as a retrospective detector of the attribution-source noun phrase rather than a lookahead for a single token.

This pole fires when the current token continues a non-English-language passage (Hindi, Greek, and related non-English text, in native script or Latin transliteration), peaking on romanized Hindi/Greek content words such as Dekhna, Bodhee, and einai/elliniko; matched English text of the same shape stays near zero.

The positive pole fires at the hinge of a value statement about a definite, measurable attribute of a concrete entity: it peaks on the last token of the attribute phrase, or of the reporting verb that introduces the value ('the stadium's capacity', 'the tower's height', 'the patient's age/gender', 'the male:female ratio', 'the company's beta', 'was recorded as', 'is expected to be'), one token before a form of 'be', 'as', '=', or the opening token of a literal value (a number, an ID or hex string), with strength scaling with how strongly that attribute term fixes the copula/value continuation. It is near zero for direct predication of an entity ('the car is red', 'the boy's mood is happy'), for non-measurable or unanchored attributes ('the arrangement is ready', 'the port number is 8080'), and at predictable non-equative continuations ('New York', 'in terms of'); the value's content never matters, and although the output direction promotes exactly that copula (' as', ' is'; Chinese 为/是) and suppresses relative pronouns ('which/who'), the measured direct ablation effect is small (lookahead KL ~3e-5), so the mechanism claim is retrospective.

Fires on the highly predictable continuation token of a verbatim-repeated boilerplate template already established in the preceding context: a C/Go brace-plus-indent or tab, an HTML/SVG/JSX tag boundary, a #pragma diagnostic word, a debug-log '/.ssh'-style path piece, or the fixed next word of an ebook-license, email-header, or institutional/collocational formula (may be, Board of, intimate partners). Long-preamble templates (ebook license, C++ signature-plus-brace, log sequence) need tens of preceding template tokens, so the same surface token in a novel, short, or single-sentence context (a fresh Python/YAML indent, an isolated bracket emoticon, everyday of/be/intimate/ssh/clang) stays quiet; a C-style indent fires whether or not its block is closed.

Retrospectively, the pole fires on the token that introduces a specific, narrow lexical value into a slot the preceding words have opened: the first piece of a rare or technical word or proper name (' sym'+'phony', ' am'+'oxic'+'illin', ' Ham'+'let', ' March', ' Celsius') or the bare leading token that Qwen's tokenizer splits off a numeral ('at 100', 'active = 1', 'Apollo 11'). It sits near baseline on high-frequency generic fillers in the same slot ('the concert', 'active = true'), on the words that set the slot up, and on ordinary prose; within the rare-word class the response is selective (penicillin, ibuprofen and xylophone stay at baseline), and a second, much larger response family on the copula after an expletive subject ('it is', 'it's', up to 7.8 in running text) is not explained by this claim.

L20/N930- is a Ruby / RubyGems detector: it is strongly active (0.3-1.0 of scale) on Ruby source code (def...end, @ivar, :symbol, #{} interpolation, bare require 'x') and on Ruby's package-manager register - gem/Gemfile/gemspec lines, the gem names rake, rspec, bundler, rubocop, jekyll and rails even inside ordinary prose, rubygems.org URLs and .../lib/ruby2.x/gems/... paths - and it reaches at most ~0.1 of scale on the same content written in Python, JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java or PHP. The pole is retrospective, not lookahead: it reads the Ruby topic already present in the context (48% of its input attribution sits more than 16 tokens back; its gate row is closest to the embeddings of 'ruby', ' Rails', 'nil', '.rb', '.erb', '#{' and 'ARGV'), and its output direction raises that same vocabulary (' gem', ' gems', ' ruby', ' rails', ' hash') in the next-token distribution rather than preparing one specific upcoming token.

Fires where a passage specifies the physical position, extent or surface of something in a concrete scene: at the spatial preposition plus determiner that open a locative phrase ('around the corner', 'off the ground', 'on the floor', 'under the surface', 'across the brook'), at the modifier that gives an object's shape or appearance ('flat surfaces', 'bare soles', 'an open backpack', 'his left shoulder', 'the muddy floor'), and at body-part terms in positional idioms ('neck and neck', 'head and shoulders above'). The same tokens in abstract, evaluative or procedural prose stay silent ('in the long run', 'the bottom line', 'the proposal', 'the theory'), even inside fixed idioms, so the pole tracks the surrounding physical description rather than the peak token: the word after the peak is irrelevant ('off the ground' 7.65 equals 'off the table' 7.65), while replacing the physical phrasing drops it ('neck and neck' 11.4 to 'tied and level' 0.4).

This pole fires on the digits of a numeral that states a quantity - a measure of how large, how far, how heavy, how long, how much, or how many something is (depth, distance, weight, duration, dose, price, or a counted magnitude with a unit or scale word such as metres, km, ug, mg, million, billion) - peaking on the digit that completes the numeral and dropping to ~0 on the token after it. The same digits used as a label or identifier (serial number, product code, store/page number) leave it inactive, and an explicit unit word need not follow: the pole reads the numeral already present in a measure phrase, it does not prepare an upcoming unit token.

Fires on a subword fragment that begins or continues a memorized multi-token word or fixed phrase: surnames after their given names (Ryan+Fredericks, David+Carlucci, Christy after a name-list comma), common words split mid-word (underst+ated, colon+ized, fed+ora, W+ob+urn, hand+-me), and encoded or path or command pieces (%+2F, &#+3, /usr/local+/lib, math+fr), with strength graded by how strongly the preceding words predict that exact completion, so the identical fragment fires several-fold stronger after its predictive prefix than after a neutral one. It stays near floor on whole-word or single-token uses of the same strings (the colon as a noun, Bog of Allen, Christ as an exclamation), on fragments of long technical words with no predictive prefix (sentence-initial Immunohistochemistry, adenocarcinoma after a determiner or adjective), and in passages containing no such fragments.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes the distinctive name of a usable system capability, product feature, or service (e.g. SOS, search, control, registration, messaging, Reporting, collision, PhotoSphere, 911, Online First) presented as something used, selected, equipped with, or offered, and stays low on ordinary object nouns (dinner, barn, salt, sparrow, manager, vacation), on the same strings used as verbs, and on artifact nouns framed as stored or contained objects (a file of receipts, a stored password or contact list) rather than usable capabilities; its output direction promotes function/feature/功能 vocabulary as a downstream category label.

The negative pole fires, retrospectively, on the token that completes a quantity pinned to an explicit scale: a non-first digit-piece of a multi-token numeral ('aged 73' peaks at '3', 'Excel 2003' mid-numeral, '90 percent' at '0', '20-30' at the final '0') or the %/magnitude word closing it ('90%', '7 billion', 'thirty years'). It requires the numeral to sit inside a scale construction: an age/demographic bracket ('aged N', 'ages A-B', 'her 30s', 'six months and older'), a version/model/rating ('iOS 6', 'Excel 2003', 'gcc 4.4', 'SPF 30'), a hyphenated range or every-N rate ('25-54', 'every 20-30 minutes'), or an N-or-more/threshold/duration frame ('50 or more', 'past thirty years'). Its gain is set by quantity-dense surrounding discourse (mean attribution distance ~84 tokens): the same construction fires weakly isolated and strongly amid other numerals. It stays near zero on opening digit-pieces, on sentence-initial bare numerals, and on numerals in non-scale uses: bare counts/scores ('73 guests', 'men scored 73', 'Thirty guests'), identifiers and calendar dates ('Room 73', 'year 2003', 'TC-3-22.20'), instruction temperatures and single times ('180 degrees', '45 minutes', 'every 45 minutes' at 2.2), and isolated bare percentages ('73% of households', '90 percent of us' sentence-initial). Residual leftovers it does not explain: bare scale nouns firing inside very numeral-dense passages ('decade' at 8.6) and large round magnitudes ('60,000', '100,000'). Its output direction promotes '+'-family continuation tokens, which together with steering (clamping emits enumerations like '100 dollars', '3 books on science, 2 books on history') indicates the pole hands downstream a to-be-continued quantity signal rather than predicting a specific next token.

This pole fires on short Italian function morphemes (di, in, ti, si, ci, tu, fu, se, ne, con, per, chi, cui, and word-onsets like Bu/ona) only when they occur inside sustained Italian text (Portuguese sustains weaker firing); the identical tokens in isolation, embedded in English/French/Spanish/German carriers, or in English translations stay near zero, and no single token is necessary since distributed surrounding context drives the peak.

N3989+ is the neuron's 'system under description' pole: it lights up over the token span where the text attributes state, behaviour, dynamics or a formal description to an entity that is being studied or modelled - 'the dynamics of the system changed over time' 9.3, 'the dynamical system has a unique attractor' 16.2, 'the behaviour of the system is described by an equation' 17.6, 'the state of the system is described by a vector' 5.6, 'the population grows according to a logistic equation' 10.3, 'the cells were grown in a dish' 6.6, 'Levy processes are a natural extension of Brownian motion' 9.2, and the scan peak 'a realistic Lotka-Volterra model with an intractable transition density' 21.2 - and it drops to baseline when the same nouns appear outside that frame (non-technical 'the team dynamics changed over the whole season' 0.1, 'a legal system has a unique structure' 0.2, technical-but-not-a-system 'the Golgi apparatus has a unique structure' 0.3, 'the model posed for the camera' 0.1, 'tomatoes grown in a garden' 0.3, 'the process took three days' 0.1) or when the clause is a bare experimental-procedure statement, which is the negative pole's job ('the specimens were randomly divided into three groups' 0.1 here vs 3.0 on the negative pole, 'completely randomized design' 0.1 vs 5.4). The pole writes the concept SYSTEM into the residual stream (Jacobian lens promotes only forms of 'system' in its top-10 at z 5.2-7.0; zero-ablating it removes probability from ' system', ' systems', ' populations' and ' process'), but its peak sits on or after the system word and does not track what follows (the same 15.5 peak precedes both 'model' and 'sentence'), so it reports that a system is being described rather than preparing a specific upcoming token.

The negative pole fires on the vocabulary of conducting and analysing a quantitative study: extent adverbs that say how completely a manipulation or measurement was carried out when attached to study nouns ('study', 'experiment', 'trial', 'data', 'sample', 'specimens' - e.g. 'a completely randomized design', 'the specimens were randomly divided into three groups') and the names of study designs and statistical procedures ('repeated measures', 'two-way ANOVA', 'multivariate analyses', 'multiple/logistic regression', 'generalized linear mixed model', 'central composite rotatable design', 'three-stage sampling', 'prospective cohort', 'doubly robust', 'orthogonal' moment functions). The same surface words in ordinary narrative or about non-study subjects, and technical vocabulary that names objects rather than quantitative procedures, leave it at baseline ('The building was completely destroyed' 0.3, 'built randomly over the years' 0.0, 'the Krebs cycle'/'the Higgs boson'/'the Golgi apparatus' ~0), and the neuron's positive pole is silent on all of these inputs (<=0.04) while its write direction is the anti-'system' direction.

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token delivers the resolving payload of a frame set up by the preceding tokens: the statement executing a just-opened code header, the predicate verb or head noun completing its subject/modifier frame, or sentence-final punctuation closing a complete proposition. It stays low on the frame-setting words themselves, and the same surface token goes quiet when its frame is removed or the unit is left unclosed.

The negative pole fires on a form of the verb 'be' (was, were, is, are, been, be, being; French est/ete) whose subject denotes an animate being: strongly for a person - a name, he/she/they, or a human noun ('the officer was' 11.0, 'the soldier was' 10.5, 'the suspect was' 9.8, 'the workers were' 9.2, 'the children were' 6.0) and more weakly for an animal ('the dog was' 5.4, 'the cat was' 5.3) - while an inanimate object, institution or abstraction as subject leaves it at baseline or in a weak middle band ('the report was' 0.0, 'the theory was' 0.0, 'the weather was' 0.0, 'it was' 0.0, 'there was' 0.0, 'the building was' 2.7, 'the company was' 5.2), and a non-'be' predicate about a person also leaves it at baseline ('the man went' 0.7, 'he said' 0.0, 'he had' 0.0, 'the suspect fled' 0.0). The same animacy response fires more weakly on animate nouns themselves, but only where the surrounding text already makes those people the topic of a statement - quantified or categorised groups ('229 patients' 10.4, '193 women', Wikipedia 'Category:People' / 'Category:Writers' lines 7-11) and objects of verbs like 'interviewed' ('the people' 8.8) - and not on inanimate nouns in the same frames ('229 samples' 2.7, 'Category:Films' 0.0, 'the samples' 0.8); its write direction promotes the forward-looking past participles (killed, arrested, injured, convicted, elected, appointed, diagnosed), and its opposite (positive) pole is weaker (scan max 8.8) and shares the be-form preference.

Fires on the token that opens the next slot of a count expression the passage has already established: strongest before a repeated 'multiple'/'Multi-' ('... may have multiple X ... may have multiple Y'; 'multiple A, multiple B and multiple C') and before the second word of a numeral range ('one or more', 'zero or more', 'one or two'), landing on the auxiliary or conjunction that opens the slot (' have', ' and', ' or', ' a', ' to', ' the'). A lone first mention of a quantity word, the quantity word itself, ordinary plural nouns and runs of 'several'/'many' stay below the active threshold (a residue of peaks on mid-word fragments of rare words, e.g. '.ro' in 'openapi.roots' or ' BRO' in 'BROOKLYN', is not covered by this rule), and the pole's write suppresses the word it anticipates: the Jacobian lens suppresses 'multiple'/'multi'/'mult' and promotes 'many'/'few'/'许多'/'muchos', and zero-ablating the pole raises p('multiple') by about 0.12 at its peak.

Qwen2.5-0.5B L21/N756+ fires on a word-internal sub-word fragment of a longer, non-lexicalised word: short letter-chunks with no leading space (' Am', ' am', ' em', ' Em', 'Ex', 'br', 'ij', ' sil', ' imp', ' aqu', ' Gre', 'astr') that begin or continue a rare name, foreign word or technical/Latinate term (Amro, Amish, amodiaquine, Rijksmuseum, silversmith, amperes, imparts, Extrême), predicting activity whenever such a fragment appears inside a multi-token word. The response is word-invariant once the fragment is fixed (' Am' = 7.3 before 'ro', 'ish', 'ato', 'ida' and 'her'; ' em' = 4.9 before 'itters', 'erald') and near zero when the same letters form a complete common word ('I am' 0.0-0.3), sit inside a single-token word ('Amsterdam', 'America', 'Amazing'), or when the passage is ordinary prose; a further 2-3x gain comes from the surrounding technical frame (identical 'at 90 amperes' scores 3.2 after 'The current was measured' but 0.3 after 'It was measured').

Retrospective: fires on content tokens written while a round bracket '(' is still open, in code or around a quoted string in prose, and is near zero for the same tokens outside any open '(' (after '=', 'print x', inside only '[' or '{', '#ifdef __X__') and after the ')' closes. Strength is tiered: about 10-21 on the name token right after '__' inside the open bracket ('getLogger(__name', 'dirname(__file', 'defined(__GNUC', 'print(g.__next'); about 4-9 on words of a quoted string inside it ('(the "License', 'log.info("... now'), on digits of an index or number argument ('i16(header[388:390', 'range(10'), and on a lone variable argument late in a snippet ('print(value' at 6.4); about 1-4 on plain identifiers in short calls or 'if (...)' conditions, and under 1.5 in prose parentheticals without quotes ('(France)').

This neuron fires retrospectively on geometric concepts, mathematical curves, coordinate geometry, and graphical plotting terminology (such as 'angle', 'triangle', 'circle', 'curve', 'slope', 'vector', and plotting verbs). It remains inactive on non-geometric everyday nouns, abstract algebra, and non-mathematical senses of words.

This pole fires on a short non-final piece of a word the tokenizer has split — a word-initial fragment such as ' ke' (keystone), ' ne' (neared, neil), ' Per' (Pervez, Permanently), ' fer' (ferocious), ' Sne' (Sneaker), ' NE' (NEAREST), ' K' (pKiller) or ' P' (Paseo), or a mid-word fragment such as 'ke' (Inverkeithing) and 'ase' (Paseo) — and on the Romance/Turkic preverbal particles 'ne', 'no', 'he', 'Não' and 'NE' that lean on the following verb, with full strength only when licensed by the immediate left context (a determiner, pronoun, title, proper name, or verb frame). It grades with that context (' ke' ~6.6 after 'the'/'a' but ~2.8 after 'mentioned'; ' Per' ~3.1 inside an assassinate-plus-title frame but ~1.6 after a bare year; whole-token 'electrical' only ~2+ inside dense technical prose versus ~1.2-1.6 everyday), and stays near baseline on single-token words with the same letters (keyboard, nearest, never, calm, Usually, john, Tuesday, Permanent, Patio, electric), on the completion tails of split words ('ystone', 'ared', 'vez', 'ocious', 'aker', 'il'), and on quoted non-ke syllables ('pa').

The negative pole fires on running legal and institutional boilerplate -- the formulaic clauses of software licences, copyright and warranty notices, contracts, statutes, regulations, and case/patent boilerplate -- and inside such a clause it is active on most of the clause at once rather than on one word, with the peak on the connective that glues the formula ('agreed to in writing' 8.3 on ' in'; 'non-transferable right to' 5.7 on ' to'; 'in any form or by any means' 5.3 on ' now'; 'Unless required by applicable law' 5.5/5.2 on ' Unless'/' required'; 'Licensed under the Apache License' 5.2 on ' Licensed'; 'not reasonably arguable' 4.6 on ' reasonably'). It falls to near zero on narrative, news, fiction, recipe, chat, academic and technical prose and on legal vocabulary dropped into an ordinary sentence ('The lawyer read the contract' 0.2; 'He put the offer in writing' 0.4 versus 'must be made in writing' 4.8), so the driver is the formula and register, not the word list; the same neuron's positive pole is complementary (it peaks on the opening piece of a rare word, ' ke' in Inverkeithing 8.7 where this pole reads 0.00, and is ~0 on licence clauses), while two weaker 1-3 responses sit outside the claim: subword pieces of rare or foreign words (' Ker' in Kerboua 5.1, ' Yak' in Yakutumba 3.3, 'In' in MacInnes 2.5, kana inside Japanese words 6.4) and the punctuation/attribute glue of code and markup ('="' 3.8, a CSS declaration ':' 3.1, '=-' in a Gradle property 4.1).

The negative pole fires on the token that completes the FIRST endpoint of a bounded span: the final digit of a date, year or number ('from September 3 ___', 'from 1966 ___ to 2015', 'June 12-14'), a day name ('Monday ___ through Friday'), or a word naming a point on a scale ('from kindergarten ___ to Grade 12', 'from their inception ___'), whenever the preceding words cast that token as an interval opening ('from X', 'between X', 'the period X', or 'X to/through/-/and Y'). The very same token falls to the noise floor when the context makes it an interval terminus ('until September 3' 1.7), a bare point in time ('on September 3' 7.6), the second endpoint of the span (<3), or a non-span 'from' ('from London to Paris' 0.5, 'from scratch' 0.0); it writes the span word 'through' into the residual stream but does not predict the connector actually chosen, since the model's own ' to' prediction is unchanged by ablating it.

The pole fires retrospectively on a token that is a subword piece split out of a longer word (the tokenizer's mid-word boundary), and its strength is set mainly by which piece it is: ' fl' (7-8 of the pole's 9.75 max after almost any lead-in), ' sul' (6.4), ' cl' (5.1), ' cav' (4.4), ' pl' (3.5), ' conv'/' sk'/' carb' (2.8) and the space/case variants ' Pl', ' Sk', 'Fl', ' Cl', plus the word-internal 'um' of 'cr|um|pled' (5.2), while the same letters inside one fused token (' flower' 0.2, ' clock' 0.4) and the leading pieces of other rare or technical words (' mitochond' 0.0, ' Elect' 0.1, ' Hyper' 0.2) stay below 0.6, so it is neither a rare-word/technical-register detector nor an air-conditioning neuron (a small residue on ordinary single tokens such as ' system' 4.7 is not covered by this rule). The word ' air' is a weak member of the same family (1.2 after a neutral 'the') that climbs to 4-9.7 only when the lead-in commits the model to a following compound head ('Please turn off the ... air conditioning' 6.5-7.3, 'the hotel air conditioning' 6.9, 'contaminants like air-borne' 5.6) and stays at 0.9-2.2 when ' air' is a plain noun or the continuation is open ('the air in the room' 1.2, 'air quality' 1.2, 'They discussed the air conditioning' 1.6).

The pole detects reader-facing service copy: it fires where a website, app, shop or company states what it does, offers or enables for its users, peaking on the connective or light function word that opens the purpose, capability or benefit clause (usually ' to', ' can', ' and', ' you', ' by', ' we'), sometimes on a word of the promise itself ('Keep', 'customers', 'better'). It is strongest (8-12) on cookie-consent and privacy-notice sentences ('We use cookies to ...', 'Our partners use cookies to ensure ...', 'This website uses cookies and similar technologies to ...'), moderate (3-6) on app, feature and benefit copy ('the app uses your camera/location to ...', 'other users can recognize you ...', 'our parties are a great way to make new friends', 'we'll keep you notified'), and weak (<2) on the very same tokens in detached narration, news and scientific reporting with a purpose infinitive ('the factory uses coal to ...', 'the committee met on Tuesday to discuss ...', 'she used a knife to ...'), so token identity alone does not explain it: 97% of the scan's 2,791 ' to' occurrences stay below 3. A weaker (<5) leftover fires on rare Greek-root technical subwords (pharmacophores, Sephadex, electroencephalography) and a few non-English function pieces.

Retrospectively fires on tokens within spans describing the physical, anatomical, or structural features and components of biological organisms, cells, or mechanical implements. It remains inactive on abstract concepts, organizations, and figurative or non-structural descriptions sharing similar syntax.

The positive pole is a topic detector for a human singing voice: it is high throughout a passage about a singer or about singing — singing-voice types and vocal technique (soprano, coloratura, contralto, baritone, falsetto, bel canto, vibrato, aria, vocals) and a person singing — and once a singer has been introduced it stays elevated for tens of tokens on otherwise neutral words (e.g. ' her' measures 11.8 after 'Maria was a singer...' but 0.0 after 'Maria was a baker...'), so it tracks the vocal-music topic rather than the trigger tokens. Instrumental or composed classical music (composer, symphony, quartet, pianist, Beethoven) keeps the positive pole near zero while driving the negative pole instead, matching an output direction that promotes ' voice'/'voices'/'sing'/'vocals'/'歌声' and suppresses 'composition'/'composed'; passages about performed or recorded sound (audio mixing, actors' performances) give only weak offshoot activation (means 1-2, peaks about 7).

The negative pole fires while the model reads a clause in which a concrete physical material - a food, drink, chemical, metal, a body or a surface - is brought into contact with, or changed by, a liquid, granular or other mass substance: 'soaked in water', 'wiped with a wet cloth', 'filled with sand', 'dissolved in water', 'stirred into the milk', 'beaten with a fork', 'filtered through paper', 'quenched in oil', 'sprayed with N2 gas'. The peak lands on the relator or verb that links the patient to its medium (' in', ' with', ' into', ' through', ' of') rather than on a fixed word class, and the pole stays at the floor when those same relators and verbs carry an abstract or informational argument ('the claim/company was dissolved', 'the report was filled with errors', 'the data was filtered', 'depends on the support of the board'), for mere placement of inert objects ('put on the shelf', 'stood against the wall'), for weather or metaphorical temperature ('the weather was warm', 'a heated debate') and for ordinary narrative prose; as an offshoot it also fires on the internal pieces of long technical or transliterated names ('Methylglyoxal', 'fluorouracil', 'Hiranyakashipu'). This is the mirror of the positive pole, whose rejected rule sat on the first token of the complement the clause was building toward: the negative pole sits on the relator inside such material clauses, and it is retrospective (its write is wasted by the time a temperature word would come next).

L21/N3648+ fires on a large expanse of sea or air named or measured as a space: ocean and sea names ('Atlantic', 'Pacific', 'Indian', 'Ocean', 'Sea'), marine features ('waters', 'continental shelf', 'coastline'), and the distances, areas, coordinates and altitudes that span them ('miles', 'nautical miles', 'km', 'square kilometres', 'degrees north'). Peaks are highest when such a space is bounded or claimed ('territorial sea', 'territorial waters', 'exclusive economic zone', 'extends 200 km', 'airspace extends 200 km'), weaker for land or generic extents measured the same way, and near zero when the same words name objects, food or abstractions ('the kitchen shelf', 'Indian food', 'Atlantic blue', '159 members', 'the economic zone'); the pole reacts to the expanse it has just read, not to an upcoming token.

The pole fires on the token where the model retrieves a specific, low-frequency lexical item rather than composing generic text: the distinctive word of a multi-word proper name (the given name after a role or institution word - 'Mayor Michael', 'Senator Marco', 'Sen. Bernie', 'Federal Communications', 'Department of', 'Court of Appeals') or the opening piece of a rare technical, taxonomic or brand word ('glomeruli', 'monopotassium', 'Lamborghini', 'Opuntia'). It sits at the noise floor on generic prose and on the same words used generically ('He met Michael', 'consumer services', 'the cells', 'a car', 'the Federal Trade Commission'); within that class strength is graded by the network's own token preference, so some familiar names in the identical frame (e.g. 'John', 'Grace') fire only weakly.

The pole fires on the token that carries the internal marker of a written clock time: the single-letter meridiem token right after the hour (' a'/' A' of a.m., ' p'/' P' of p.m., as in '3 a.m.', '9:00 p.m.', '8 P.M.'), the ':' or '.' right after the hour number ('3:30', '16.00', '6.45 in the morning'), or the 'o' of "o'clock" (and, more weakly, the 'A' of a dotted era marker after a year, '476 A.D.'), when the preceding number is read as a time of day. It does not fire on a bare hour with no marker ('at 3 tomorrow'), on the merged 'am'/'pm'/'AM'/'PM' tokens, on a meridiem with no hour in front of it ('in the a.m.'), or on the same letters and separators where the number is a ratio, score, price or version ('3:1', '3.14 dollars', 'Version 2.0'), an item label ('item 3 a'), or an ordinary word ('parley', 'Barking', 'Epigraph').

The negative pole is the active regime of a bilingual 'appraisal' concept neuron: it fires when the running text names an evaluation of something — a rating, judgment, verdict, review/reviewer, evaluation, appraisal, award or acclaim (Chinese 评价/评分/评级) — peaking on that word or on the function word one or two tokens after it (e.g. 'The [[rating]] was', 'a rating [[of]] four and a half stars', 'Two [[reviewers]] independently'), and stays near zero for process/reporting vocabulary (audit, inspection, measurement, analysis, report) and for neutral description even in identical frames. It is retrospective, not lookahead: its output direction demotes exactly the vocabulary it detects (rating/evaluation/criteria rank 4/8/15 in w_out·W_U and are suppressed with z≈-12, while its 'promoted' list is the bottom of the same unembedding ranking), the classic Voita suppression signature, so it does not prepare an upcoming token.

L21/N4242+ is a retrospective detector of a specific family of Greco-Latin word stems, and it fires on the subword piece that carries the stem when Qwen's tokenizer has split the word: 'throm' in thrombosis (7.2), 'orph'/'morph' in morphological (9.9), 'otyp' in phenotypic (4.0), 'orph' in polymorphisms (6.6), 'phot' in photonic (8.7), ' hom' in homonym (10.4) and homologation (11.4), 'emp' in spatiotemporal (4.5). It stays at baseline on the same word written as one token (' morphology' 0.1, ' phenotype' -0.2, ' orientation' 0.6, ' vulnerability' 0.0, ' voltage' 0.5), on the pieces that follow the stem ('onym', 'osis', 'onic', 'ages' about 0) and on other split technical words that are not in the family ('polymer' -0.1, 'hydro' -0.3, 'capac' 0.3, 'hepat' -0.9), and for stems that also occur as whole words the model's own expectation that the word continues gates it ('The volt is the unit...' with P(next token is a word-piece) 0.73 fires at 12.1 while 'a nine volt battery' at 0.003 sits at -0.3; 'the path through...' 0.56 fires at 3.4 while 'the garden path...' 0.02 is 0.5).

The pole marks a word-building fragment: it peaks on the leading piece of a long technical/Graeco-Latin word that Qwen's tokenizer splits into several tokens (' dermat'+'ology', ' therm'+'odynamics', ' cardi'+'ologist', ' electr'+'ify', ' pen'+'itenciário', ' democr'+'ático'), and the strength is carried by that fragment token itself - it barely changes with what completes it (dermatology, dermatologist and dermatitis all give ~10.9/12) and the completing pieces stay near 0. Everything the tokenizer keeps whole (psychology, voltage, thermometer, electromagnetic, and every ordinary word) and rare non-technical fragments (tungsten, obelisk, archipelago) stay below ~0.1 of max, and at the fragment the pole's write promotes the pieces that would finish the word (dermat->'ology'/'itis', magnet->'ometer'/'ism'/'ron', therm->'ite'/'os'), so it tracks an unfinished technical word being spelled out of pieces rather than a topic or a specific upcoming token; engagement is stem-specific (e.g. ' pharmac' and ' onc' are weak), so not every technical word engages it.

The pole fires on passages whose subject matter is the mind and the brain: the entities and claims of neuroscience and cognitive psychology (neurons, synapses, hippocampus, cortex, dopamine, memory, attention, perception, emotion, language, psychiatric and neurological disorder). Substantially weaker but still above threshold, it also rises on scholarly discourse about the arts and sciences (universities, departments, professors, disciplines, papers and citations), while matched passages about commerce, finance, law, engineering, machines, plants or everyday events - and the same words in a technical sense, such as a computer's memory or a company's working capital - stay below a quarter of peak. Because the receptive field is a whole phrase of roughly 20-40 tokens, the single highest token is usually a function word (of, the, in, and, or) or a sub-word piece inside such a passage rather than a fixed trigger word.

The negative pole is a definite-article feature: it peaks on the token 'the' (' The'/'the') in running prose - roughly 5-9x stronger than 'a', 'that', 'this' or 'one' in the same left context - with its strength set by the preceding span (0 in some documents, up to 11 in content-dense particular-reference passages such as 'from the top of the tower at Pisa' or 'for the war'; it is not explained by the article's own probability, rho = -0.19, or by next-token entropy, rho = 0.04). It additionally fires on a small lexical set of word-initial sub-word tokens that begin long content words (' Her', ' Ple', ' Gre', ' Middle', ' clar', 'am'), which fire on token shape rather than meaning (' Her' scores identically in Herod and in Heron).

This pole fires retrospectively when the current token delivers or terminates a conventionally constrained factual detail set up by the preceding 1-3 tokens: a fixed-phrase or collocation completion ('world' after 'Hello,', 'fell' after 'stock market', 'images' after 'captured'), a quantity with its unit or a digit inside a year/code dimension, a name/date/place specification ('Nairobi' in a capital list, 'March', 'sea level'), or the closing punctuation, bracket, or newline of a clause carrying such content. The same surface trigger token stays quiet when the licensing local pattern is absent: generic emotion words or pattern-breaking substitutes ('purple', 'tables', 'joy') in the identical slot collapse the peak.

Litigation-procedure neuron: once a court-case context is set up (case caption, opinion or filing naming parties such as the State, the defendant or an appellant), it fires on the token that opens or sets up a party-role or filing term. Examples: the 'Pl' piece of Plaintiff in a caption or at a paragraph start (~10-15), ' a' or ' "' after '[litigant] filed' before motion/notice (~7-10), a litigant subject like 'The State' or 'the Department' before filed/moved (~7-8), and APPELLANT'S before MOTION (~9). The same tokens without legal context, and ordinary legal prose away from such slots, stay weak (<~2). Leftovers it does not explain: German articles and negation after a verb (keine/eine, ~7) and Android XML 'android:layout' (~4-7).

The pole fires on the singular nouns that name an institution's own activities and the things it funds, teaches and delivers - research, training, teaching, learning, curriculum, course, service(s), programme/program, project, placement, study, survey, assessment, evaluation, screening, prevention, intervention, treatment, therapy, development, expansion, delivery, funding, grant, policy - and on the multi-word institutional names built out of them (Strategic Research Action Plan, Family Violence Prevention Services, Tobacco Regulatory Science Program, Office of Naval Research); each such noun carries roughly 1-4 by itself and the whole clause around it rises to 3-11 once several of them fill it, so sustained programme, prospectus, grant-call or service-description prose runs hot over whole clauses including the intervening function words. What changes from the administrative-register reading is that the trigger is this lexical class and not the text's administrative or public-service character: civic and procedural administration is now predicted inactive (minutes, tenders, contracts, invoices, budgets, ballots all measure 0-0.6), as are the generic umbrella nouns scheme, initiative, strategy, provision and management (0.2-1.0 even inside an institution frame), commercial and consumer copy, sport and recipe uses of the same words, financial reporting and narrative fiction (all 0-1.2), and a lone field noun dropped into otherwise unrelated prose reaches only about 1-2.8, below the 2.49 line; the 6-10 spikes on word-internal fragments of rare proper names (' N' in Nooksack, ' En' in Envisat, ' py' in pyrenaica) are a separate token-level effect, not this claim - the same fragment reaches only 2.2 in a stand-alone sentence and needs an already-hot encyclopaedic passage in front of it to reach 10.

The pole fires when the current token is the lexically informative content word that satisfies the syntactic slot set up by the preceding one to three tokens (head noun after a determiner or possessive, main verb after its subject noun or pronoun, copula after a complete subject, second half of a fixed collocation, or token closing a clause or code block), and stays low on function words that leave the phrase incomplete. It therefore predicts which occurrences of common tokens fire (e.g. the clause-boundary comma but not list commas, the copula after a full subject but not auxiliaries mid-phrase), which token identity alone cannot.

This pole marks the cultural sector: it fires on words naming the institutions that produce and transmit culture - schools, colleges and universities, teachers; newspapers, magazines, journals and broadcasters; books and publishers; film, cinema, theatre and museums - while the same-sized, same-frequency institutions of other sectors (bank, hospital, army, factory, ministry, court) and concrete objects (building, road, window) leave it at zero in the identical frame. The drive is passage-level as well as lexical: the same word fires several times harder inside an arts/media/education passage than inside a finance or manufacturing one (identical sentence, 3.84 vs 0.95), and the neuron writes the culture concept forward (zero-ablating it removes 1-2.7 nats from 文化/'cultural'/'art' at every peak and the tokens it loses most are library, film, newspapers, Book), which is what the Jacobian lens is reading.

Retrospective particle-physics detector read out at the following low-content token: the pole peaks (2 to 8.5, against a scan maximum of 8.24) on a preposition, article, conjunction, comma or first fragment of an unfamiliar word when the word just before it names a subatomic particle or particle process ('in'/'the' after electrons, protons, neutrons, photons, quarks, gluons, mesons, kaons, bosons, hadrons, leptons, neutrinos, positrons, antiprotons, atoms; 'into' after annihilate; 'on' in 'based on cavity QED'), and it falls back to the floor when the particle word is instead followed by another content word, so 'The mesons in the box were counted' peaks at 6.4 while 'The mesons were counted in the box' peaks at 1.7. In the identical frame everyday, biological and clinical nouns leave it at the floor ('The cats / kidneys / cookies / onions / crayons in the box were counted', 0.2 to 0.6), clinical and abstract-mathematics words are actively suppressed ('coronary' -3.0, 'the' after 'eigenvalues' -2.3), and in addition a handful of rare name-like tokens carries a fixed positive response (' O' 5.6, ' U' 1.4, ' Ar' 3.1, ' Toyota' 3.1, 'silver' 1.8, ' classical', ' non', ' solar', ' optical'), which is why the fragment ' Ar' fires in 'Gregg Araki' (3.1) but the fragment 'Tan' does not fire in 'Gregg Tanaka' (0.0).

Retrospective: Qwen2.5-0.5B L22/N2281+ fires on a token that does not end its word - the next token continues the same orthographic word with no space - so its peaks land on the word-initial or word-medial BPE fragment of a long or rare word ('[[counter]]|int|uitive', 'electro|card|[[i]]|ogram', 'oph|[[thalm]]|oscope', 'gastro|[[enter]]|ology', 'Long|[[le]]|at', 'm’|[[app]]|elle', 'am|[[oxic]]|illin', 'pharmac|ological' peaking on 'pharmac'), and it falls back to the floor on that word's final fragment ('...|ogram', '...|ological', '...|oscope' all read 0.0) and on words the tokenizer keeps whole however rare they are ('notwithstanding' leaves the whole prompt at 0.25 and 'nevertheless' at 0.08), with ordinary prose usually at 0.15-0.4 against a 0.45 active threshold. It prepares no single upcoming token (Jacobian lens flat, kurtosis 3.3, promoted list '_BACKEND'/'=R'/'ruc' incoherent; zero-ablating the pole moves probability toward sibling word-internal fragments such as 'okin' after 'pharmac' and 'ogram' after 'echoc', KL 2e-5, far below the protocol's lookahead threshold), and which long technical words fire is only partly predicted - echocardio-, pharmaco-, gastroentero-, otorhinolaryngo-, cholecyst- and counter- words fire while spectro-, photo-, immuno-, histo- and arteriosclero- words of the same shape do not - that residue, and the fixed ~0.16 the pole reads on a document's first token, are left unexplained.

N2511+ fires on the token that sits inside a literal, format-determined string rather than a composed one: code formatting runs (' {\n', '{\r\n'), markup/URL syntax ('{ref-type=', 'xmlns:', '.com/en-us'), LaTeX or math fragments ('_n', '-P'), numeric/identifier literals introduced by a format label ('7' after 'ISBN:', '3' in 'sha384-'), escape runs ('\u0'), French elision clitics (' d'', 'qu'', 'l'') and memorised patent/legal formulas ('invention relates to', 'incorporated herein by reference', 'more particularly'), and it grows with the amount of such formatted context preceding it. The same tokens in composed prose stay near the floor (plain ' incorporated', 'xmlns', '-P', '/en', ' relates' and 'ref' all < 0.7), plain code without such a literal and Italian/German prose stay <= 1.7, and zero-ablating the pole at its peaks leaves next-token probabilities essentially unchanged (KL 3e-5 to 1e-3), so the pole is retrospective.

N2511- is a foreign-script detector: it fires on the current token when the text around it is written in a script the model has almost no training data for, and the response builds over the run, so a single character of a very low-resource script is enough even inside an English sentence (Kannada 'ರ' 40, Bengali 'ক' 48, Devanagari 'न' 39, Khmer 'ក' 37, Tamil 'அ' 31, Burmese 25-35, Georgian 'მ' 26, Armenian 'ա' 21, Amharic 12), a real Greek word of 5+ letters reaches 12-31 ('Ελλάδα' 26, 'Παρίσι' 23, 'και' 20) while isolated Greek letters and nonsense Greek letter strings stay at 0.5-6, and well-covered scripts never fire even in normal runs (Russian/Ukrainian/Serbian Cyrillic <=3, Arabic/Persian <=2.4, Hebrew 0.6, Chinese/Japanese/Korean/Thai/Vietnamese <=1.5); it also ignores emoji, rare CJK or Hangul glyphs, accented Latin (<=1.3), IPA and maths symbols, and English rare words, typos and nonce strings (<1.6), and only rare archaic letters inside well-covered scripts reach the 5-10 tail (archaic Cyrillic 'ѨѩѪѫ' 10). Far below that (2-8, under the active threshold) it responds to ASCII tokens sitting in a run of code/markup/LaTeX notation - a LaTeX backslash or the ' math' fragment inside \mathbb/\mathcal, import-path heads ' android'/' java', an attribute ':' or a tag boundary '"><' - and to romanised Indic proper nouns (2-5), while a lone markup line, the same words in ordinary prose, and its positive pole's format-literal tokens stay <1; zero-ablating its peaks barely changes next-token probabilities (KL 0.03), so it is retrospective.

Retrospective detector of literal, vivid descriptions of physical scenes and bodies in motion. It fires on the concrete noun, or on the 'nearly/almost' + motion verb, when a natural object or body part does something physical: strongest on the literal word 'sun' (the sun came up/rose/set), then on things like branches pushing through a roof, eyebrows/heart 'nearly' touching or stopping, an eagle's wings 'and soared', waves 'crashed' on rocks, leaves 'rustled', and on 'fast' in the stock phrase 'X is fast approaching'. It stays near zero for the same words in non-physical, figurative or institutional use ('the band came up', 'Sun Microsystems', 'over the moon', 'raining cats and dogs', 'moving fast.', 'nearly finished the report') and on technical or administrative text; sporadic peaks on mid-word subword pieces of rare words (capecit|ab|ine, Gurt|ov|oy, Danish ' ø|konomien') are leftovers that this hypothesis does not predict.

The negative pole is a retrospective detector of unfamiliar, non-whole-word material: it fires on the token where the surrounding text has pulled the model out of ordinary English - a sub-word fragment or short word-initial fragment of a long, rare, technical, transliterated or foreign-language word (Dutch, Turkish, French, Japanese, Latin/Greek genus names, chemical names) that has to be assembled from pieces instead of retrieved as one familiar token. It is near zero on ordinary English words in ordinary prose, and the same token fires or not depending on the surrounding language (' transparent' = 4.3 after 'Het bestuur moet more' but 0.0 after 'The board must become more'), with a secondary peak on the first token of a document (1.5-5.3) and on a few English words that head proper-noun phrases (' Foreign', ' Public').

The pole fires on clinical maternal-newborn-child-health writing: obstetric/perinatal passages (fetal/foetal, fetus, neonatal, congenital, gestational, prenatal/postnatal, intrapartum, postpartum, preeclampsia, placenta, umbilical, amniotic, Apgar, preterm birth, low birth weight, small-for-gestational-age, neonatal jaundice/sepsis, perinatal mortality) and child-health disease/deficiency statements (vitamin A or iodine deficiency, measles mortality, malnutrition), with strength rising as such clinical content accumulates. It is inactive on adult/general medicine (hypertension, cancer, diabetes, infections) and on lay or non-clinical text; ordinary proper names (Smith, Obama) do not fire, and the isolated strong peaks on the rare name-initial fragments ' V' (Vargas, Valesky) and ' W' (Waddell) are a separate token-level residue outside this reading.

The pole is a retrospective word-piece (spelling-fragment) detector: it fires when the current token is one of a small family of short subword fragments - the two-letter onsets ' ch', ' st', ' Ch', ' St', ' sh', ' ph' and mid-word pieces such as 'ph' in triphosphatase - i.e. a piece the tokenizer has split out of a longer word rather than a complete word. In a fixed carrier the fragment token alone sets the strength (' ch' 7.2 > ' st' 4.4 > ' sh' 2.0 > ' ph' 1.3 > ' pl' 0.8 > ' br' 0.6, identical across chisel/chive/chasm/chaff), and the pole stays at its floor on words held in one token (cheese, church, station, strong, photon, stanza, child), on longer fused pieces carrying the same letters (' perm' in permanganate, ' Neb' in Nebuchadnezzar, ' chlor', ' chem', ' Chunk' in getChunk), and on function words and punctuation.

At the first position of the input this pole is a graded opener detector: code openers (class/import/def) drive 7-9.5, connective or article openers (The/But/Because/Sh) drive 1-3, and pronouns, question words and most other openers drive ~0, while the same tokens placed mid-sentence in plain English prose evoke ~0. Within quoted dialogue and French spans it instead stays active across many tokens and spikes on straight-punctuation-adjacent fragments: the elided pronoun in j'habite (9.7, versus 3.3 for unelided il and 0 for the same elision in an English frame), the auxiliary did after she inside quotes (2.4), and mid-word pieces such as ochond in Mitochondria; its output direction promotes ASCII structural tokens and strongly suppresses curly-quote tokens, consistent with marking spans where straight-ASCII punctuation applies.

The positive pole fires on a non-final sub-word piece of an organic-chemistry or carbohydrate name: a word-initial or word-internal fragment (including hyphen-led pieces such as '-c', '-gl') that the next token continues without a space, inside a name of a compound, functional group, ring or reaction: ' en'|olate/antioselective, ' lact'|one, ' gly'|colysis, ' gluc'|ocorticoid, ' fr'|uctose, 'cyclo'+'hex'|ene, 'metallacy'+'c'|lobutane, ' but'|enes, '-c'|oupling, 'nucle'|otide, ' al'|dehyde. It is silent on whole-word tokens (including chemical words that are one token, ' ketone', ' ester', ' acid', ' sugar', and the same letters as complete words: ', but', ' en route', ' con artist'), on the word-final piece ('one', 'ose', 'ine'), on ordinary prose, and mostly on clinical/biomedical vocabulary ('cyto|chrome', 'ery|thema' stay below threshold); recall rises with the density of chemistry in the context (a lone 'fructose' in plain prose is silent). In a full-corpus 512-token rescan, about 80% of tokens above 25% of max were such pieces (62% plain alphabetic pieces plus hyphen/slash-led pieces), firing 28x more often than whole-word tokens; the leftovers are a minority of fragments of rare proper names or words (' Al'|cazar, 'Pell'|egrini, ' b'|arked, ' g'|lockenspiel) and a few function words inside a dense carbohydrate-chemistry passage. Retrospective: its output promotes ' constraint(s)'/' restrictions', unrelated to the continuation pieces.

The negative pole fires on the token where the context makes a constraint/restriction word the likely continuation (e.g. ' budget'→' constraints', ' impose a'→' barrier/limit', 'self-im|posed', ' keep her mouth'→' shut', ' locked and the windows'→' locked'); restriction vocabulary that does not set up such a continuation (' not allowed to', ' reveals a fundamental') leaves it silent. Its output suppresses ' constraint(s)'/' restrictions' logits (Jacobian lens, kurtosis 9.2), so it acts as a final-layer suppression/calibration neuron for constraint words; zero-ablation moves KL 0.037 but not concentrated on specific tokens, hence claimed retrospective.

Fires retrospectively on text whose vocabulary is about plants in the garden/botany/produce sense: the peak lands on the tokens of plant-cultivation words and their immediate neighbours (' shr' in 'dwarf shrub tundra' or 'weeding the shrubs', ' tub' in 'potato tubers', ' vegetable' in 'vegetable beds', 'alled' of 'walled garden', 'eding' of 'weeding', ' watered', ' pot' of 'potting shed', the token after 'the seeds of'), growing with how much of the passage is cultivation content, while the same neuron's positive pole promotes and this negative pole's output writes out that garden token family (' garden', ' vegetable', 'leaf', ' planting'; suppressed z = -10.6, kurtosis 7.3) - a Voita-style suppression write, not lookahead, since the promoted side is incoherent noise. It stays inactive (peak below ~3 on this pole's 12.1 scale) on non-botanical senses of the same word forms (decision tree, chemical plant, random seed, seed capital, family tree, square root, table leaf, dog bark, Garden of Eden), on plant-free registers (steppe/glacier terrain, farm work, legal, politics, arithmetic, non-English garden text), and on lone commercial mentions ('vegetable boxes for market', 0.18 of scale).

The negative pole fires on the last token of a bracketed insertion - the token immediately followed by the closing ')', ']' or '}' - when an earlier bracketed insertion in the same passage was closed and followed by a comma, i.e. when the insertion is a non-first item of a comma-separated series of parentheticals (the '2' of 'Alpha (1), Beta (2), Gamma (3)'; the '6' of 'Items [4], [5], [6]'). It is inactive on a lone parenthetical in ordinary prose, on the first insertion of a series, on an insertion introduced by 'and' rather than a comma, and on plain text containing no bracketed insertion.

L23/N1769+ is a retrospective 'Java-family member declaration' unit: in Java, Kotlin, Swift, Dart, Scala and Java-style C# source it peaks on the token that opens a declared member - a field modifier (private, public, static, final), a method or constructor name just before its '(', a ':' or '->' introducing a type, a ',' or '<' inside a capitalised parameter or generic list, or the indentation that begins the next member or statement line - and its write suppresses the built-in type tokens it expects ('String', 'Math'). Activation is primed by the members already written in the window, so the first field of a class body scores 3-6, the second and later members 8-10, and full Java/Kotlin/Swift class bodies reach 8-17; sparse Java-shaped code still fires at 3-6 (a Rust struct/impl, a C# class written with lowercase 'string', a Java method body containing a for loop and println calls, a JavaScript function of arithmetic assignments, the same class written with lowercase types), while Go, C, C++, PHP, Ruby, Python, TypeScript classes and interfaces, plain JavaScript without a Math call, SQL, shell, HTML, JSON, YAML and prose stay at or below about 2.5.

Fires on a short non-word fragment token, usually one containing h/H/sh or the piece 'unt', that opens or interrupts a common word split into unusual subword pieces, so the word is left unfinished and its completion is strongly determined (Stone|h|enge, Aft|ersh|ock, "|h|undreds, four| H|DMIs, | CH|B, | unt|reatable/oward/amed, fo|resh|adow, | Sh|rink, | wh|istfully). It stays near zero on whole-word tokens, on the completion pieces themselves, on ordinary single-token words containing h, and on name or foreign-word fragments such as Ash-, Kh-, Bh-, Ch-, Hy-.

Fires on an opening or boundary token after which a fresh word will start with no leading space: strongest (10-12) when such a non-word token is the very first token of the text ('[', '
', '

', '---
', '{
', '"'), and moderately (3-10) mid-text on a line or paragraph break that ends a title, question or label (':

', '?

', '.
') or on an opening ' (' / ' [' / ' "' that starts a parenthetical or quote. It is near zero on word tokens, including a first token that is a word ('The', 'So'), and on any token followed by a space-prefixed word (e.g. ',' or ' ' in place of the break). Its output promotes spaceless word-start fragments ('sc', 'sm', 'g', 'gl') as a broad class, not specific tokens.

Fires at a position where the model is partway into a proper name or word and must continue it with the next token, strongest (about 0.4 to 1.0 of max) when the continuation is a TV/radio broadcaster name, Japanese or US networks above all. Examples are ' T' before 'BS' in 'Fuji Television and TBS', 'テレビ' before 朝日/東京, '（' before テレビ in Japanese programme credits, ' and' in 'NBC, CBS, and' and ' i' in 'BBC iPlayer'. It is also strong on a lone word-initial letter piece of a tokenizer-split word, mostly p/P/T ('H+-p|umps', ' P|uts', ' p|acted', ' p|21'); complete words, standalone letters ('p < 0.05'), most other initial letters ('b|umps', ' H|ikes') and lists of non-broadcaster companies stay near zero.

Fires on the first piece of a word the tokenizer has split, a short fragment that is not a word by itself and must be continued by a suffix piece. It is strongest when that fragment is a lone r/R or w/W (also U), especially right after a hyphen or slash ('re-r|outed', 'most-w|atched', 'nerve-r|acking', ' R|OLLBACK', ' UR|GENCY', ' r|ica', 'men/w|omen'), and also fires on short non-word stems such as ' rep|umping', ' typ|ologically', ' sw|ivel', ' Str|asbourg'. It is near zero on complete single-token words (' top', ' rebooting', ' ENERGY'), on the continuation pieces themselves, on fragments starting with most other letters (' p|obre', '-h|ated', '-s|orted', ' H|ORIZONS'), and is weaker when the same word already appeared earlier in the text. Unlike the positive pole, which fires partway into broadcaster and other proper names, this pole tracks the opening fragment of an unfinished common word. A secondary case is ' Best' opening an award category ('nominated for Best Picture').

The pole fires on tokens that belong to source code rather than natural language: components of whitespace-free identifier, path, URL and markup-name runs - '/db' in django/db/__init__.py, 'js' and '/ajax' in js/ajax/addQuiz.php, ' android' in android:textColor, 'id' in @+id/imageView4, 'load' in luaotfload, 'nonatomic' in @property (nonatomic,) - with strength rising with the length and separator density of the enclosing run (10-34 for long runs containing / _ : = -, mostly under 2 for short or standalone ones). It is near zero on natural-language words even inside the same file (comments, string literals, HTML body text), on separator-only tokens such as '="', '/', ':', ';' and on the same words written out as prose, and its output only weakly promotes generic code continuations (':text', '/image', '/button', '>\n') rather than one specific next token, so the mechanism is retrospective.
